claims.boundary: The acquisition supplies descriptive full-register records without an admitted dependence model or confirmatory selection procedure. Activity and repetition-delay contrasts do not establish causation, physical shot alignment, or cross-PUB order.

claims.statement: The three complete 4096-shot nominal-one Tuna-17 jobs establish all 12 selected realized predictable destination-response cell contrasts within 0.10, with all 12 baseline endpoint intervals within 0.10, under the frozen simultaneous 99% martingale contract.
claims.boundary: The endpoint covers marginal early/final cells on declared qubits 4, 11 and 6 and one nominal preparation. It establishes neither physical populations, QND readout, causal destination dependence, full-register invariance nor projector geometry. The old six-job endpoint remains unavailable; the zero/one comparison is retrospective. Further hardware requires another approved case accounting for measured waits and benchmarking context.
assumptions: Trusted chronological binary shot records, coherent provider/local timestamps and the declared inverse decoder.
Conditional-response targets and finite-sample uncertainty follow the frozen three-job mathematical contract; transient bounds remain unverified.

claims.statement: The approved six-job destination comparison stopped at its 3600-second request deadline after three nominal-zero submissions. All 12,288 submitted shots were retained in 14.356782 reported execution seconds with zero charges; the frozen whole-case decision is implementation route unavailable because the nominal-one acquisitions are absent.
claims.boundary: Operational incomplete-case outcome. Read-only recovery collected the third already submitted job after the executor stopped. The whole-case equivalence/departure endpoint remains unavailable; further submissions require a separately approved case.
assumptions: Provider timestamp fields and result identities describe the recorded service operations.
The frozen complete-case decision requires both nominal preparations.

claims.statement: In the retained posthoc nominal-zero prefix, q6 terminal-one counts are 938, 2525 and 969 out of 4096 before, during and after rotation; the maximum empirical early/final joint-cell contrast is 0.43896484375. The q4 and q11 maximum contrasts are 0.0052490234375 and 0.001708984375.
claims.boundary: Descriptive frequencies from the incomplete case. A transformation restricted to stored early labels leaves each dataset terminal marginal unchanged; broader reconstruction/scheduling changes and a coincident transient remain alternatives. Neither statistical acceptance of the six-job case nor physical causation or populations is established.
assumptions: The documented rightmost classical-bit-zero convention supplies the decoder.
Stored source identity establishes transport bytes, while served analog schedules remain unavailable.

claims.statement: The approved permuted repeat on qpu:ascella (job 6ef8e8db) ran job-00's 64 circuits, all 64 compiled circuits equal to job-00's, in ANU QRNG order at 16384 samples per iteration: 1048576 samples in 186 s, job-00's duration, for 1.032768 free credits, and all 27 endpoints qualify again. Under the preregistered comparison the outside-block clicks follow the execution sequence, not the setting: per-setting Spearman against job-00 -0.075 (p 0.56), lag-1 autocorrelation -0.653 in the new order (p below 1e-4), compiled-phase change Spearman 0.12 (p 0.35), and the median count grows with the budget (log2 ratio 0.83). The per-setting analyzer residuals reproduce, Pearson 0.974 on X and 0.802 on Y (p below 1e-4), at contrast 0.9719 against 0.9699 on X and 0.9669 against 0.9702 on Y.
claims.boundary: Two jobs six hours apart on one device; the alternation's physical mechanism (which acquisition stage alternates) and the configuration error behind the reproducing residuals stay unidentified. Permutation p-values assume exchangeable positions under the null; the budget reading compares medians of two jobs. Equal total durations of jobs six hours apart in different orders assign no marginal time to the further samples, because no record separates acquisition from overhead.

claims.statement: In both Ascella signed-coherence runs the statistics computed from the returned compiled circuits lie within 2.2e-4 of every registered ideal, while the block-conditioned X and Y statistics read 0.97 to 0.98 times their ideals and the direct readout 1.004 times; inverse-variance weighted gain-and-offset fits leave X chi-square 195 and 408 on 18 degrees of freedom and Y 44 and 110. Of the five linear relations a setting-independent complex gain imposes on the sign-odd coefficients, X0 + Xc2 = 0 fails in both runs on the projected simultaneous intervals (-0.028 and -0.030) and the rest hold except Xc2 + Ys2 in job-01. Pooled per returned compiled configuration, job-00's X and Y values predict job-01's within counting noise (chi-square 3.3 and 8.3 on 10) where job-00's gain-and-offset fit does not (402 and 106). Outside-block counts follow the catalogue dark profile only at high amplitude: quartile-pooled profiles differ (likelihood ratio 407 and 921 on 21), and a two-component Poisson fit places the alternation (lag-1 -0.65 to -0.71) in a catalogue-shaped component holding most of them, beside a component on modes 4 to 9 that alternates weakly. physical_perf reads 0.0209 in every iteration of different outside-block counts.
claims.boundary: Exploratory fits without preregistered thresholds; the multinomial errors ignore drift within an iteration, and the configuration agreement sets no equivalence margin on drift. The dark profile uses plan-time catalogue rates, the two-component fit is descriptive (its deviance has no asymptotic reference, its fitted profile differs between the runs, and its job-00 catalogue share exceeds the bound the pooled composition sets), and no detector gating model converts a component's amplitude into acquisition time. The diagnostics records' residual_chi2 and block_less_dark_share verdicts carry no inferential reading; response-geometry.json holds the weighted fits.

claims.statement: Fitted on job-00 and scored on job-01's pooled configuration statistics, no preregistered shared error family of the returned 12-mode Ascella meshes passes (X and Y p > 0.01 on 10 degrees of freedom with predicted X0 + Xc2 inside job-01's interval). Homogeneous independent Gaussian heater phase noise (sigma 0.022 rad), a uniform heater gain, nearest-neighbor thermal crosstalk, a uniform coupler offset and homogeneous coupler noise leave held-out X 527 to 663 and Y 167 to 241 and predict X0 + Xc2 of -0.005 or above against job-01's -0.031 [-0.048, -0.013]. Shared static heater offsets reproduce X0 + Xc2 (-0.022, -0.025) but leave held-out X 53 and 39. Supplementary static heater and coupler offsets together pass job-01 (X 7.0, Y 12.6 on 10), a test of reproducibility across acquisitions; prediction of left-out configurations is claim ascella-signed-coherence-configuration-holdout.
claims.boundary: Shared families of the provider's returned mesh model only; the multinomial ignores drift within an iteration, the in-block background uses plan-time catalogue dark rates and each job's own outside-block counts (about 2e-4 on the predicted statistics), and the covariance is the inverse expected information for the low-dimensional families and the observed information at the posterior mode for the static ones. Static offsets come from pure-state propagation. The job-00 in-sample statistics are descriptive. The detector-efficiency and coupler-offset families and the leave-one-configuration-out test were added after the preregistered table and decide nothing; the record's left-out statistic starts each fold from the full-data mode and scores it in counting variance only, and ascella-signed-coherence-configuration-holdout supersedes it. The rejections hold for each family in the form fitted and exclude no correlated or drive-dependent error. The fitted families replay within 1e-3 relative plus 1e-8 absolute across BLAS builds.

claims.statement: Refitted on job-00 without one configuration from the zero start, so that neither the start nor the mode selection reads the left-out counts, no static offset family of the returned Ascella meshes predicts the left-out configurations' X and Y statistics within counting plus fitted-prediction variance: the standardized sums over the 10 scored configurations of each readout read X 205, 167, 87 and 27 and Y 88, 45, 36 and 52 for heater offsets (tau 0.1, 0.3), coupler offsets (tau 0.1) and both together, each family at 30 or more on X or Y, against the returned mesh's 343 and 75. The combined family's X predictions carry a median prediction variance 12.7 times the counting variance, so its X sum reflects weak identification and its Y sum the shortfall. In counting variance alone the training-only folds give X 257 to 535 and Y 109 to 1114.
claims.boundary: Static families of the provider's returned mesh model only, with pure-state propagation and the block light unclipped (configuration-holdout.json, built with the light clipped at 1e-9, holds one combined-family fold in a local mode 4.36 higher in negative log posterior); the prediction variance is the local quadratic approximation at each fold mode, the folds share 28 or 29 training configurations, so the sums are descriptive and carry no chi-square reference, and the reading criterion (30 or more on 10 keeps the shortfall) was fixed in plan ascella-configuration-holdout-training-only before the run. The analysis was added after the preregistered table and decides nothing; it does not show that the underlying errors are independent between configurations or exclude a correlated or drive-dependent shared error. The fitted families replay within 1e-3 relative plus 1e-8 absolute across BLAS builds.

claims.statement: Refitted on job-00 without one configuration from the zero start under the training-only folds, a drive-dependent heater family of the returned Ascella meshes (tau-0.3 heater offsets plus one slope per heater on the returned phase as drive, prior width 0.1) leaves the left-out X statistics at a standardized sum of 36.1 and Y at 24.8 over 10 configurations each, against the returned mesh's 343 and 75, so the X sum keeps the shortfall under the 30-on-10 criterion fixed before the run. Its X predictions carry a median prediction variance 10.4 times the counting variance (Y 2.1), and in counting variance alone it gives X 474 and Y 186.
claims.boundary: One drive-linear heater family of the provider's returned mesh model, with pure-state propagation; the drive is the returned phase in [0, 2 pi) with its zero at 0, because the passive phase that sets each heater's wrap point is absent from the returned circuit, and per-heater wrap points, quadratic drive terms and crosstalk through the phase-voltage matrix lie outside the family. The prediction variance is the local quadratic approximation at each fold mode and the folds share 28 or 29 training configurations, so the sums are descriptive and carry no chi-square reference. The family, its prior width and the reading were fixed in plan ascella-configuration-holdout-training-only before the run; the analysis was added after the preregistered table and decides nothing. The fitted family replays within 1e-3 relative plus 1e-8 absolute across BLAS builds.

claims.statement: A per-heater drive-dependent phase error of the returned 12-mode Ascella meshes (shifted Legendre polynomials of the drive to order 1 or 2, or 1, cos and sin of the returned phase to order 1 or 2; 252 to 630 coefficients under N(0, tau^2) priors) reproduces job-00 and job-01 (job-01 held-out X 4.0 to 5.4 and Y 6.7 to 12.6 on 10, X0 + Xc2 -0.026 to -0.028) but predicts no left-out configuration it can be judged on. Refitted from the zero start on the training configurations alone, the order-1 polynomial keeps the shortfall on X (standardized sum 32 on 10, Y 28), and the four richer families predict with a median prediction variance 6.5 to 485 times the counting variance and sums of 1 to 15, so these data leave them undetermined; in counting variance alone every family does worse than the returned mesh (X 386 to 564 against 343, Y 94 to 225 against 75).
claims.boundary: Families of the provider's returned mesh model only, with the background, multinomial and pure-state propagation of the static fits; the training-only folds, the prediction variance as the local quadratic approximation at each fold mode and the reading criterion (30 or more on 10 keeps the shortfall, below 20 with a median variance ratio above 1 reads as weakly identified) are those of plan ascella-configuration-holdout-training-only, fixed before this run. The folds share their training data, so the sums are descriptive and carry no chi-square reference. The families were added after the preregistered table and decide nothing. The posteriors hold several modes and the one an L-BFGS path reaches follows BLAS and SIMD rounding, so the record is written under the OpenBLAS Haswell kernel and numpy's x86-64-v3 dispatch that ci/run_gates.py and ci/pr_checks.sh set, and replays within 1e-3 relative plus 1e-8 absolute under those kernels.

claims.statement: For every n >= 3 and distinct nonzero i, j < 2^n, the associator phase g_ij of W_ij = L_{e_i e_j}^dagger L_{e_i} L_{e_j} has algebraic degree exactly max(1, bitlen(max(i, j)) - 2), independent of n: each phase splits as A(y) + c xi over the top index bit with c = N(i') + N(j') + N(i' ^ j'), a pair with an index in the top half has A = g' + delta_u + delta_v + const with u != v, and the census adds 3 2^(b-2) (2^(b-1) - 1) pairs of degree b - 2 at bit length b (84, 360, 1488, 6048, 24384 at dims 16 to 256).
claims.boundary: Written induction (slice Lemma D, involution Lemma A, two-point Lemma B); scripts/cd_phase_degree.py checks every identity on all ordered pairs and the statement through n = 8, and the machine-checked claims cd-associator-anf-rocq and cd-associator-census-rocq prove the statement and the census in Rocq for every n. Walsh spectra within one degree, which the degree does not determine, stay with scripts/associator_walsh_classes.py.

claims.statement: For n >= 3, 0 <= m < 2^(n-2), i = 2^(n-1) + m and j = i + 2^(n-2), the associator phase is g_ij(x) = x_(n-1) + delta_m(z) for m != 0 and N(z) for m = 0, with z the low n - 2 bits of x, so W_ij is one multi-controlled Z on the low n - 2 qubits conjugated by X on the zero bits of m, times at most one Z and a global sign, while its positive-polarity ANF has 1 + 2^(n-2-popcount(m)) or 2^(n-2) - 1 monomials.

claims.statement: Each of the 360 degree-3 dim-32 associator phases is l1 l2 l3 + q with l1, l2, l3 linearly independent linear forms on F_2^5 and deg q <= 2, so W_ij = D_q U_A^dagger (CCZ x I) U_A; the cubic part takes 15 values, 24 pairs each.

claims.statement: For all 360 dim-32 cubic pairs the factorized Design C circuit (block barriers kept), the Reed-Muller diagonal oracle and the CCZ normal form equal diag((-1)^omega) entry by entry, global phase included; on the ibm_kingston coupling map (optimization level 3, seed 11) they compile to about 122-131, 10-43 and 25-32 CZ on average, and the normal form uses fewer CZ than the diagonal oracle on 97 pairs.
claims.boundary: One coupling map, one seed, ideal semantics; the two diagonal circuits encode the predicted phase and are references for the factorized circuit, not substitutes. The dim-16 ripple circuits have no cubic phase.

claims.statement: The CCZ normal form cuts the associator circuit by 18.9 percent of its CZ gates, raises fidelity 1.19x, and is a verified drop-in replacement for the factorized circuit.
claims.boundary: The counts were typed-in estimates, the equivalence test compared CCZ with itself and a singular U_A, and a diagonal built from the predicted phase cannot replace the circuit that tests composition.

claims.boundary: The kernel printed SNR 0.0 against the expected 1.18e-03; two sampled arms at SNR 2 need 4/dP^2 shots in total, about 2.9 million (about 750 s) at 50 Hz, and IBM guarantees no PUB order, so one job does not interleave matched pairs.

claims.statement: Ramsey on 20 defective and 20 clean triples detects a sedenion-structure-dependent detuning down to about 5 kHz.
claims.boundary: The single-quadrature fit returned -29.5 kHz for +30 kHz, and no circuit is named in which a triple label sets a qubit frequency; bright and dark members differ in one virtual RZ.

claims.statement: A pre-delay sweep has 11 percent power to detect a photonic contribution to the 84/84 contrast, a negative result.
claims.boundary: The power restates hand-set inputs (a 0.01 kHz shift at 0.1 contrast per kHz against a 0.02 standard error); it measures nothing about the device.

claims.statement: On the executed Fez ripple atlas circuits and IBM's executed pulse times, a static frame detuning per qubit, resimulated at its leave-one-out fitted values, predicts held-out edge fringe phases better than the lane mean on six of seven lanes (0.086 to 0.120 rad against 0.129 to 0.238 rad); the fitted detunings are mostly 5 to 30 kHz, up to about 60 kHz.
claims.boundary: Inferred from one run's fringe phases; the detuning model's linear held-out residuals stay 1.8 to 3.0 times its leave-one-out noise floor, lane 0 is unexplained, and only a direct measurement such as conditional Ramsey confirms per-qubit detunings.

claims.statement: On the executed Fez and Kingston ripple atlas circuits at IBM's executed pulse times, six coherent error families (frame detuning, CZ conditional phase, static ZZ in the partner-in-0 and symmetric frames, SX amplitude and axis tilt) fitted one at a time to the edge fringe phase offsets of all 14 lanes leave every lane except two (Fez lane 5 with axis tilt, Kingston lane 2 with detuning and with partner-in-0 ZZ) above 1.5 times its leave-one-out noise floor under every single family, the lowest ratio per lane ranging from 1.68 to 3.70, so no single family accounts for the offsets; partner-in-0 ZZ scores below the symmetric frame on 13 of 14 lanes in the linear fit and on all 14 resimulated, by a median factor of 2.4, and is the best single family on 7 lanes (detuning on 4, axis tilt on 3), while SX amplitude beats the lane mean on none.
claims.boundary: Inferred from one run per backend; the best single family per lane is an after-the-fact selection among six, and the lane-4 ranking of the evidence README selects among eighteen models, so no family is confirmed, and a confirming test scores one named model on lanes it was not selected on. Each Kingston lane excludes two edges that span a calibration identity change. The partner-in-0 frame is physical if IBM calibrates each qubit frequency with its neighbors in |0>, which no repository source states; conditional Ramsey with the partner in |0> (proposed-conditional-ramsey-hamiltonian) measures the frame directly. On lane 4 the edge-to-edge contrast deficit stays at 2 to 2.5 times its floor under every phase-fitted model.

claims.statement: Under the ibm_kingston noise model of 2026-10-15T19:42:21-07:00, the compiled factorized dim-32 Design C circuit (about 123-128 CZ) keeps the two spectral classes apart at 20,000 shots: collision estimates 0.1807-0.2534 for the 234 pairs of ideal K = 11/32 and 0.0933-0.1135 for the 126 pairs of ideal K = 5/32; the Reed-Muller and CCZ normal-form references keep about 86 percent of the ideal gap.

claims.statement: Replaying the executed circuits of 14 retained IBM runs under every retained calibration of their backend, at each member's executed shot count, the noise model reproduces the recorded replay distances to sampling precision (mean |ghost - recorded| 0.0077 TV over 206 replicas against 0.0079 TV between two independent ghost draws), the predicted distance to hardware moves by only 0.001 to 0.032 TV across calibrations against floors of 0.026 to 0.435 TV, and today's calibration fits the old data better than the execution-time calibration by more than two standard errors on 10 of 14 runs. Five 2026-10-18 Kingston runs and one further Kingston snapshot, added by an incremental merge, widen the calibration spread to as much as 0.054 TV (2026-10-12T055624, 0.088 to 0.142), and the exact-law n21 members and the 149-member control runs reproduce their recorded replays within 0.0027 TV. A second merge adds ten 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-20 runs and six snapshots: the four init-control runs whose every job ended in ERROR are skipped, and the six that returned shots reproduce their recorded replays within 0.0056 TV, their predicted distance moving by at most 0.008 TV across calibrations. A third merge adds the two 2026-10-21 segmented sweeps and two snapshots: both reproduce their recorded replays within 0.011 TV, and their distances to hardware (0.509 and 0.451 TV) stay near the one-line model's limit, which no readout factor closes (part_f).
claims.boundary: Calibration identity explains little of the mismatch; whether the model underestimates noise is not settled (today's CZ error is higher on 9 of the 13 kernel runs that play CZ, while readout changes correlate with the opposite sign), and an error-scale sweep per run is the test.

claims.statement: Driving a Tuna-17 neighbor with 40 X gates inside an 800 ns target idle shifts the target's idle phase by up to 0.633 rad (Q7 on Q4) and 0.695 rad under simultaneous drive (Q7 and Q8 on Q4), against undriven idle phases of -0.03 to -0.12 rad; the pairwise residual phi(AB) - phi(A) - phi(B) + phi(none) departs from zero beyond |z| = 3.29 on targets 3 (z = -3.38) and 11 (z = -3.43) and stays within |z| < 2.1 on targets 0, 4 and 12, and conditioning a target on its driver's final outcome leaves its phase within a few hundredths of a radian. The QX reference reads residuals of 0.012 to 0.077 rad against a 0.044 rad sigma.
claims.boundary: The circuits, shots and qubit roles were fixed in cases.json before submission, while the analysis (phase-domain residual, driver and conditioning fields, every threshold) was fixed after the data arrived; the batch's five jobs (four additivity configurations, then teleport) ran sequentially about 11 s apart, so drift between jobs is not cancelled and enters every cross-job difference; each star and each path occupies its own qubits, so every value is a per-star or per-path input and forms no device-wide average; the counts carry no state-preparation or readout correction; one 16384-shot run on one Tuna-17 calibration. A ZZ phase from a driver's time-averaged excitation during its X train is not separated from a drive-induced Stark shift.

claims.statement: The Quantum Inspire Ry emulator returns qubit 0 as the leftmost outcome character: an X on q[0] of a two-qubit circuit with no bit register read `10` in all 1024 shots, the reverse of QX and Tuna, which put qubit 0 rightmost. The transported-pair teleport circuit, with a bit register and measurements, failed at execution with an empty log and the message 'error interpreting cQASM script'.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 the exact Clifford+T Design B witness of (e1 + e10)(e4 - e15) = 0 has raw P(s = 0) = 0.471 [0.466, 0.475] dark, 0.512 [0.508, 0.517] bright and 0.499 fixture over three regions in a Latin square, an endpoint contrast of 0.042 (4.2 % of ideal, 6.5 % of Kingston's 0.646) with dark below bright by about 13 standard errors; the raw pooled fixture agrees with 1/2 (z = -0.42); the endpoints straddle 1/2 with midpoint 0.4915, so dark + bright - 1 = -0.017 (z = -5.3) rejects the preregistered shared symmetric-contraction model; the region on qubits 0, 1, 2, 4, 5 shows no resolved contrast (0.002, 95 % -0.009 to 0.013); the QX twin reads 0, 1 and 0.490.
claims.boundary: One 16384-shot run per circuit on one Tuna-17 calibration; three sequential Latin jobs leave case contrasts exposed to between-job drift. Every dark and bright replica uses 66 CZ and 26 T; each fixture uses 70 CZ and 26 T. Kingston used about 45 CZ and continuous rotations, so endpoint contrasts compare implementations as well as devices. The corner fixture uses selector Q4 while its endpoints use Q2. The preregistered raw tests reject one shared symmetric contraction, not all depolarizing descriptions or any uniquely identified coherent, non-unital or coupler mechanism. The all-zero/all-one readout calibration includes preparation error and omits readout crosstalk under the witness state.

claims.statement: On the noiseless QX emulator the readout ring-down dry run reports 'not detected' on both series under the preregistered rule: all 10 targets are usable at visibility 1, every |delta(tau)| is at most 13.6 kHz against 4.7 kHz standard errors, chi2(H1) runs 0.25 to 10.96 on 5 degrees of freedom (60.3 on 50 summed over targets), and the largest chi2(H1) - chi2(H2) is 6.02, below the 13.82 threshold. QX returned its 10-character measurement register for circuits declaring bit[20], so the mid-circuit outcomes were absent and the postselected cross-check did not run.
claims.boundary: An ideal state-vector emulator at 2048 shots per circuit, one run per circuit in 18 batches; it tests parsing, submission, collection, the analysis and the decision rule on data whose answer is zero, and establishes nothing about Tuna-17's readout, its register width or the postselected cross-check. The decision rule was fixed in the cases before submission; the all-shot estimator replaced the postselected one after these data showed the measurement register, which changes no circuit byte and leaves the rule's text unchanged, and on these data the two coincide because no mid-circuit bit returned.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 series P (targets Q0, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q16, 8192 shots per circuit) the preregistered rule reports 'not detected': 7 targets are usable (Q5 fails the 0.3 visibility floor), 3 classify as tails (Q6, Q10, Q16) and 2 as static offsets (Q11, Q12), below the 50% threshold. No classified target fits H2 (chi2 30.7 to 193.7 on 3 degrees of freedom); Q11's readout arms sit 19 to 33 kHz below its reference at every tau out to 2 us.
claims.boundary: One series on one device state, read against its batch-00 calibration as the rule fixes; Q6's visibility of 1.08 shows that calibration no longer describes Q6 after the 04:12Z platform calibration, so its class rests on a stale correction. The rule compares H2 with H1 and tests neither model's fit, so the tail and offset classes mark arm-to-arm structure beyond shot noise rather than a residual-photon decay. P-05 and P-06 stay outside the analysis because they straddle the 04:04Z q9 change; the reruns replace them.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 series Q (targets Q1, Q2, Q3, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q13, Q14, Q15, 8192 shots per circuit; delays d = 2 and d = 77) the preregistered rule reports 'not detected': 7 targets are usable (Q7 and Q8 fail the 0.3 visibility floor), 3 classify as tails (Q9, Q14, Q15) and none as a static offset, below the 50% threshold; Q15's tail class holds under the all-shot estimator only, and its postselected estimate classifies as none. Q9 fits H2 (chi2 6.95 on 3 degrees of freedom) while Q14 (146.8) and Q15 (39.3) do not; Q14's readout arms sit 43 to 61 kHz below its reference from tau = 100 ns out to 2 us.
claims.boundary: One series on one device state, read against its batch-00 calibration as the rule fixes; Q15's visibility of 1.28 to 1.46 shows that calibration no longer describes Q15, so its class rests on a stale correction. The rule compares H2 with H1 and tests neither model's fit, so a tail class marks arm-to-arm structure beyond shot noise rather than a residual-photon decay. The postselection check bounds the shift from discarding mid-circuit-outcome shots at |z| <= 4.2 (Q13).

claims.statement: Tuna-17 returns the full bit register: bit[34] circuits on qubit[17] came back as 34-character strings carrying every mid-circuit outcome. On 2026-10-17, Q9's idle P1 rose from 0.02-0.05 to 0.27-0.29 from 04:06Z and stayed there through 05:33Z, and after the 04:12Z platform calibration Q0 and Q6 prepared in |1> read 0.39 and 0.14 after a 2 us wait (0.85 and 0.67 at 03:39Z) while their idle P1 stayed below 0.04.
claims.boundary: Readout-calibration circuits that idle 2 us before readout, so P(0|1) folds 2 us of relaxation into the assignment error; the platform publishes no calibration, so a change is located only to the interval between two retained batches.

claims.statement: Q9's elevated idle P1 on Tuna-17 from 04:06Z on 2026-10-17 is misassignment of |0> that leaves the qubit in |0>. Same-batch idle and X readouts bound, at one-sided 3-sigma binomial limits, e0 >= 0.19 in the three zero-wait batches (0.145 with a 2 us wait) against e0 <= 0.030 before the change, and the excited population p <= 0.115. In series Q at zero delay, shots whose opening readout of Q9 gave 1 end an X90 pair at the level of opening-0 shots: excited fraction w = 0.021 +- 0.013 over 2122 opening-1 shots, where the other eight targets read -0.10 to 0.20.
claims.boundary: The bounds assume p <= 1/2, an X that inverts at most fully and idle and X readouts from one batch; the herald test reads the zero-delay arm, because relaxation during a longer delay pulls w toward 0, and its opening readout is a mid-circuit readout taken with nine targets read at once, at 04:39Z.

claims.statement: After the 04:12Z platform calibration of 2026-10-17, the zero-wait P(1|1) of Q0 and Q6 at 05:26-05:33Z keeps 0.55 and 0.16 of the excited scale read before the change, and that loss is not relaxation inside the 800 ns readout: relaxation would need T1 <= 1.36 and 0.44 us and leave P(1|1) <= 0.156 and 0.015 after a 2 us wait, where the 2 us wait runs read 0.389-0.393 and 0.140-0.144 (z >= 32).
claims.boundary: Assumes the device is unchanged between the 2 us wait runs (04:15-04:24Z) and the zero-wait runs (05:26-05:33Z), and that a qubit surviving the whole readout window reads 1 at the pre-change scale, which bounds T1 for any discriminator response.

claims.statement: P1 after X X with no wait, beside a readout-0 and readout-1 pair in one Tuna-17 batch, separates an under-rotated X from |1> misassignment on Q0 and Q6: under-rotation by the angle their zero-wait P(1|1) implies predicts 0.98 and 0.52, misassignment 0.038 and 0.013. Ramsey inverted with the matched calibration cannot separate them when X and X90 share the under-rotation, because the raw quadratures then take the readout-scale form sin^2(beta) (1 + cos phi) / 2; a fault confined to native X keeps the X90 Ramsey at the earlier scale, which Q6's raw quadrature mean (0.064 against a floor of 0.148) excludes and Q0's (0.287 against 0.175) does not.
claims.boundary: The predictions use the 05:26-05:33Z state; Tuna recalibrates between user jobs, so a run first checks that its readout pair still shows the fault, and leakage, whose X train plateaus instead of oscillating, needs X trains of three and more.

claims.statement: The Ry emulator rejects any bit declaration, assigned or not ('error interpreting cQASM script'), and fails a measure statement at compilation ('not in the primitive gate set'); X, H, CNOT, Rz and an asm(Rydberg) INIT block run, with outcome distributions within total-variation distance 0.035 of the ideal at 1024 shots.
claims.boundary: Two-qubit circuits, one run each on the emulator as served on 2026-10-17; widths above two qubits and other constructs are untested.

claims.statement: In the pre-T0 batch on Tuna-17 (4096 shots per circuit, jobs finished 15:38Z) the Q0 and Q6 readout fault of the morning is absent: Q0 reads P(1|1) 0.973 and Q6 0.957 against the precondition limits 0.7 and 0.3, and Q9 reads P(1|0) 0.018, so the precondition reports fault-recovered and the double-X discriminator is not read. Every qubit of the admitted layout {1, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14} passes the T0 readout rule (readout-1 P1 0.912 to 0.975, readout-0 P1 at most 0.045), and q5, q6, q7 and q9 are readout-admissible; q5, q6 and q7 keep their Ramsey visibility exclusion.
claims.boundary: One batch on one calibration, taken after the platform benchmarking the operator observed at 15:34Z; the readout state can change at the next calibration. The double-X P1 values it records (Q0 0.019, Q6 0.110) are not a discriminator reading, since the precondition failed, and the proposed discriminator claim proposed-tuna17-q0-q6-double-x-discriminator stays untested. Readout admission lifts no visibility exclusion.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 the reduced two-label LCU of edge (1,10)(4,15) of kite 3, corrected per batch with its own readout pair, keeps a contrast C(1) = 0.954 +- 0.003, C(5) = 0.857 +- 0.003 and C(9) = 0.710 +- 0.003 over a 3 x 3 Latin square of pairs {(1,4), (10,13), (12,14)} and batches at 16384 shots, so the per-CZ retention is r = 0.9654 with 99% bootstrap interval [0.9638, 0.9671], inside the decision band [0.87, 0.97] as preregistered and above its prediction [0.87, 0.96]. The depth-1 upper bound 0.961 clears the 0.5 floor, so the program continues; C(1) and r both miss their predictions ([0.72, 0.82] and [0.87, 0.96]) upward. The QX twins of the three witness circuits read every replica's predicted outcome in all 2048 shots.
claims.boundary: One calibration, three pairs and one edge; the dark replica of each depth sits on one pair and batch, so C(n) carries that pair's offset, and a pair x depth interaction stays inside r. The upward miss of C(1) comes from the prediction, which carried the selector's raw readout factor (about 0.87) while C(n) is readout-corrected; 0.82 / 0.874 = 0.94. Every bright replica cleared the depth-1 bright floor.

claims.statement: Programs of H, CNOT, Z, S, X and Rz on up to 9 atoms run on the Ry emulator when they carry no bit register and no measure statement, the cause of the earlier 'error interpreting cQASM script' failures. Shallow reduced-LCU replicas (one CNOT) read their ideal outcome at a fraction of 0.978 or more and the P = 1/2 replicas sit inside |z| < 4.5; the 9-atom teleport program R9 completes with 77 of 1024 shots (7.5%) outside its ideal support; the full Design B witness of (1,10)(4,15) reads P(selector = 0) 0.270 dark and 0.656 bright, a contrast of 0.387, below the 0.9 ideal-fraction floor, so the smoke series stops there as an emulator rate.
claims.boundary: One run per circuit on the emulator as served on 2026-10-17 at 1024 shots; the Ry error model is undocumented, so the loss with depth is reported as an emulator rate and never as an algebraic result.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 the packed follow series (7 batches, 21 jobs at 16384 shots, readout brackets in batches 0, 3 and 6 that moved at most 0.0076) gives every preregistered decision the census predicts. The reduced two-label LCU classifies all six rows: the kite-3 edge D = -0.964, -0.953, -0.916 on (1,4), (10,13), (12,14), its kite-6 twist D = +0.967, +0.952, the strut D = 0.001 (SE 0.002 to 0.004). Twist equality holds in all four block x setting crossovers at shot noise without a pair allowance: |Delta| at most 0.0040, |z| at most 2.44 against 3. Every depth-1 X conditional coherence has the census sign (E_0 = -1 bright, E_1 = +1 dark), and all eight strut branch expectations lie inside 0.1 + 3 sigma. Both associator walks read <X_c> with the sign of omega = -1 (-0.784 +- 0.006 on star 14 {11, 12, 16}, 6 CZ; -0.937 +- 0.006 on path 4 {1, 2}, 4 CZ), their omit-last controls stay inside 0.1 + 3 sigma, and the walk magnitudes 0.819 and 0.938 lie inside 0.10 of T0's r^n_CZ (0.810, 0.869). The five QX twin batches read every deterministic replica's outcome in all 2048 shots.
claims.boundary: One calibration of one evening (23:08Z to 23:29Z), three pairs, one edge, its twist and one strut, and two walk exemplars. The twist test differences replicas of one batch, so drift between batches cancels; the classification and coherence signs are deterministic-limit decisions that the batch-to-batch scatter of the exploratory claim does not reach. The cross-predicted magnitudes are reported, not decided: two depth-1 X coherences on (10,13) read |E| = 1.10 after readout correction, outside the 0.954 +- 0.10 band, because the bracket's e10 for q13 exceeds its witness-context value (claim qi-tuna17-boxkite-follow-ladder-drift).

claims.statement: The follow series' reported estimates and their limits on Tuna-17. Coherence ladder (CZ depths 1, 5, 9; unweighted fits, 99% shot-noise intervals): r_coh = 0.962 and 0.957, r_pop = 0.925 and 0.915, r_coh / r_pop = 1.040 and 1.047 on (1,4) and (10,13); on (12,14) r_coh = 0.908 while 2 Pc(9) - 1 is negative, so r_pop is undefined; the phase slope per CZ lies within [-0.008, 0.008] rad on every pair. The X and Y replicas of one depth-9 bright edge, which run in consecutive batches and share the selector marginal, differ by 0.024 to 0.033 on all three pairs (4 to 7 shot-noise sigma), against at most 0.014 at depth 5 and 0.007 at depth 1, so deep-circuit populations scatter between batches by about 0.03 beyond shot noise and the ladder intervals understate the uncertainty; r_coh / r_pop above 1 and Pc(12,14, depth 9) = 0.483 below 1/2 are not established. Against T0 seven and a half hours earlier (no retained record places a platform calibration between them), the bright-edge populations moved by -0.209 on (12,14) at depth 9, -0.106 on (10,13) at depth 5 and -0.042 on (1,4) at depth 9, beyond that scatter. The q13 readout-1 bracket gives e10 = 0.091 while the bright (10,13) coherence's raw -0.911 corrects to -1.105, so the all-qubit readout pair misstates q13's |1> misassignment in the witness context. The walk controls carry phases of 0.297 +- 0.010 rad (star) and 0.052 +- 0.009 rad (path) about omega. The 21 jobs executed in 243.3 s against the design's 233.6 s.
claims.boundary: Descriptive summaries of the retained follow runs; nothing here was a preregistered decision. The bootstrap carries shot and readout-bracket noise only. The q13 discrepancy has two candidate mechanisms that this design does not separate: readout that depends on the state of neighboring qubits (readout-1 excites all 17) and a preparation error of readout-1's own X on q13. The walk phases identify no CZ window or detuning, since each CZ adds its residual local phase. The path omit control reads -0.119 against a limit of 0.126 and one strut branch +0.135 against 0.136: inside the preregistered null offset, though far from 0 on shot noise. The retained shot order carries a 50 Hz modulation that grows with CZ depth (claim qi-tuna17-shot-record-50hz-line), so the ladder's decay mixes decoherence with a time-averaged oscillating phase. A within-batch ladder demodulated at the line is the prospective test of r_coh / r_pop.

claims.statement: The retained per-shot outcome lists of Tuna-17 jobs carry a line at the 50 Hz grid frequency in wall-clock time. A band scan at 0.019 to 0.021 cycles per shot finds the line (whitened, p below 1e-6 after the band's look-elsewhere factor) in 72 of 159 Tuna-17 jobs and in none of 113 QX jobs, none of 51 readout circuits (readout-0, readout-1 and the context readouts, at up to 131072 shots) and none of the 8 depth-1 LCU circuits; it appears in Ramsey, CZ-ladder, walk, additivity and Walsh-exemplar circuits, with first-harmonic amplitudes in P(1) up to 0.43 (q7, ring-down Ramsey) and 0.39 (q5, coupler-ZZ Ramsey). Across the readout ring-down arms, whose circuits differ only in a wait of tau cycles of 20 ns, the peak frequency rises with tau at 50.4 +- 4.0 Hz (31 jobs, one intercept per batch): 12.6 standard errors from the 0 Hz a shot-index-locked source predicts and 0.1 from 50 Hz, which at 50 Hz puts one shot at 402.9 to 404.6 us in the ring-down circuits and 400.7 us in the follow series. In the follow series the bright-edge selectors on (1,4), (10,13) and (12,14) oscillate with amplitudes 0.19 to 0.26 at CZ depth 9, 0.09 to 0.13 at depth 5 and below 0.0175 at depth 1, in phase across the three pairs (resultant 0.996 to 1.000 per job). Within-job stationarity (16 block means per bit, the smallest per-bit chi-square tail times the bits scanned) falls below 0.01 in 11 to 33 percent of the box-kite pre-T0, T0, follow and Walsh-exemplar jobs and in 61 to 75 percent of the morning ring-down jobs. The detection statistic whitens the scanned bits by their same-shot correlation matrix, so correlated bits of one shot do not inflate it.
claims.boundary: A reanalysis of retained shot order, which the platform does not document as temporal; the wall-clock slope is the evidence that it is. The mechanism is inferred, not measured: a 50 Hz modulation common to the chip that grows with the phase a circuit accumulates (wait or CZ count) fits mains-frequency interference on the qubits' frequency or the flux pulses, but no retained probe separates flux pickup from any other 50 Hz path, and the third-harmonic amplitudes do not separate a 150 Hz component from the nonlinear response to a large phase swing. A time-averaged oscillating phase lowers a job's mean contrast, so the follow ladder's decay rates and r_coh / r_pop mix decoherence with this modulation. The scan detects lines in one band only.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 the |1> misassignment of q13 depends on the preparation context of the chip: e10 reads 0.0895 and 0.0863 with all 17 qubits excited (readout-1, batches 0 and 6) against 0.0441 and 0.0399 with q1, q13 and q14 alone excited and every coupled neighbor in |0> (readout-iso-x), differences 0.045 and 0.046 at about 45 standard errors, so context is established on q13 by the preregistered rule (above 0.02 and 5 SE in both brackets). It is absent on q1 (-0.0009, -0.0016) and q14 (-0.0027, -0.0006). The preparation path is absent under the 0.02 threshold on all three: e10 after H Z H minus the interpolated isolated e10 is +0.016 (q13), +0.005 (q14) and -0.0002 (q1). Corrected with the readout-1 brackets, the depth-1 X conditional coherence on (10,13) reads -1.104 and -1.060 (batches 1 and 4); corrected with q13's isolated e10 it reads -0.997 and -0.955, within one of the physical bound; (12,14) reads -0.995 and -0.994 with readout-1 and -0.999 and -0.995 with q14's isolated e10. The follow series' unphysical -1.105 on (10,13) is therefore a calibration artifact of the all-qubit readout-1 bracket applied to q13.
claims.boundary: One device state of one night (01:55Z to 03:02Z, 2026-10-18) at 131072 shots per job. readout-1 and readout-iso-x differ both in the neighbors' state at measurement and in the X pulses applied to the neighbors, so the design does not separate state-dependent readout of q13 from drive crosstalk of those pulses on q13's preparation; readout-1 also excites q10 and q11 together, so it does not say which neighbor matters. The preparation differences below the 0.02 threshold are significant on shot noise (q13 +0.016 at about 20 SE, q14 +0.005 at about 9 SE) and are reported, not decided. Beside an excited q13, q10's own e01 rises by 0.011 to 0.014 against readout-0 (reported).

claims.statement: The within-batch Latin-square ladder on Tuna-17 (every circuit holding CZ depths 1, 5 and 9 on the pairs (1,4), (10,13) and (12,14); X batches 1 and 4, Y batches 2 and 5; 131072 shots per job) gives rho = r_coh / r_pop above 1 on all three pairs in both X batches: 1.021 and 1.020 on (1,4), 1.021 and 1.022 on (10,13), 1.005 and 1.006 on (12,14), each 99% interval excluding 1 (preregistered decision: above 1). The replicate difference exceeds 3 combined standard errors on (12,14) only (z -3.85; (1,4) 1.59, (10,13) -2.68). r_pop is 0.951 to 0.957 on (1,4), 0.953 to 0.958 on (10,13) and 0.976 to 0.978 on (12,14) across all four Latin batches. The 50 Hz line is detected in all 12 Latin jobs, as predicted; the depth-9 over depth-1 amplitude margin holds in 10 of 12 jobs and is refuted in the two jobs whose depth-9 pair is (12,14) in batches 4 and 5 (batch-04 latin-x-1 and batch-05 latin-y-1), where that selector's first harmonic falls to 0.0027.
claims.boundary: rho above 1 means the population contrast decays faster than the joint coherence, which neither a global depolarizing channel (rho = 1) nor dephasing (rho below 1) gives; a coherent error that moves selector population, or the 50 Hz modulation averaged over a job, would raise it, and the design isolates neither. The preregistered rho uses the readout-1 correction, which overstates q13's e10 (claim qi-tuna17-boxkite-ladder-readout-context); with every iso qubit's e10 from readout-iso-x, rho reads 1.021 and 1.020 on (1,4), 1.020 and 1.022 on (10,13), 1.005 and 1.006 on (12,14), each 99% interval again excluding 1, so the decision is the same under both corrections. The line refutation is of the preregistered first-harmonic margin; the second harmonic of the same selector stays at 0.020 to 0.022 (claim qi-tuna17-boxkite-ladder-drift-harmonics), so the refutation does not show the modulation absent.

claims.statement: Descriptive readings of the ladder series. Against the follow series about two and a half hours earlier, the bright-edge populations rose by 0.071 (1,4), 0.092 (10,13) and 0.394 (12,14) at CZ depth 9 and by 0.003, 0.035 and 0.190 at depth 5; (12,14) at depth 9 moved from 0.483 to 0.877. The (12,14) selector at depth 9 carries a first harmonic of 0.024 and 0.026 in batches 1 and 2 and 0.0027 in batches 4 and 5, while its second harmonic stays at 0.020 to 0.022 in all four (shot-record lock-in at each job's peak). In the shot-record scan the 21 ladder jobs fall below an adjusted block-stationarity p of 0.01 in 52 percent of jobs, and none of the 9 readout circuits carries the line at 131072 shots.
claims.boundary: Descriptive; nothing here was a preregistered decision. A first harmonic that vanishes while the second persists fits a static phase moving onto an extremum of the selector's response, inferred, not measured. No retained record places a platform calibration between the follow and ladder series; batch 4 waited about 30 minutes in the queue.

claims.statement: On sim:belenos (its default noise model g2 0.003, indistinguishability 0.92, transmittance 0.06) the six S1 box-kite circuits reproduce their exact Q(sqrt2) ideals: bright a = 1 (5003/4996/0/0), dark a = 0 (Wilson upper bound 0.00038), strut a = 0.506 against 1/2, the one-hot 16D dark pair 0 clicks on all 16 algebra labels, and two-photon label fractions of 0.472 (edge) and 0.0134 (strut), whose strut inversion gives V = 0.918 against the simulator's 0.92.
claims.boundary: One job per circuit on sim:belenos as served on 2026-10-17; the simulator applies its own noise model and Quandela's transpiler, so agreement shows the cases, runner and compilation path are correct, never that hardware reaches the ideal.

claims.statement: On qpu:belenos the bright block that sim:belenos reproduces exactly, sent as a 4-mode unitary inside a 24-mode identity and compiled to the same 552-beam-splitter circuit, keeps 0.470 (Wilson 0.460 to 0.480) of one-click samples on its four modes, and of those an algebra share a = 0.256 (0.244 to 0.269) against the ideal 1; the leaked clicks fall mostly on modes 14 to 19, whose dark counts are below 0.2 per second.
claims.boundary: One 10000-sample job at the 2026-10-17 calibration (HOM 92.6 %, g2 1 %). The root-cause record (docs/evidence/quandela/belenos_leakage_rca.json) refutes a circuit, encoding, convention or multi-photon cause: the decoded compiled mesh reproduces the ideal, and no single-parameter error model reaches the shot-noise floor; the exact replay after a calibration reproduces the leak, and 64 random meshes of the same session show errors about a fifth the size the leak needs, so the leak stays specific to this job's form or mesh.

claims.statement: On sim:belenos an iterated job runs every iteration for one credit and compiles each iteration separately (eight distinct meshes in one fringe job); the edge block's fringe over phi = k pi/4 has visibility 0.996 and offset -0.008 rad and the strut block's is flat (visibility 0.023), and the bright block sent as a compact 4-mode unitary, compact native gates or 24-mode native gates reads a = 1 each while every form compiles to the full 552-splitter mesh.
claims.boundary: Five sim:belenos jobs on 2026-10-17 under the simulator's default noise model; they establish the job, iteration and compilation behavior of the service, never hardware performance.

claims.statement: Quandela Cloud re-transpiles every circuit sent to sim:belenos, the Belenos architecture with its 574 phases bound per iteration (job 1d7160c1, 16 settings) and the same architecture as a numeric circuit (job e5b74123): every returned computed_circuit changes all 574 phases and keeps only the occupied input column (|U|^2 within 2e-4), each setting's histogram lies within shot noise of its ideal (TVD 0.0002 to 0.038 at 1500 samples), and the efficiency-weighted likelihood computed on the returned meshes names the ideal model 352 nats ahead of coupler noise.
claims.boundary: Two sim:belenos jobs on 2026-10-17 with perceval-quandela 1.3.1 against a platform running 1.3.0 and exqalibur 1.4.2; the served meshes match exqalibur's CircuitOptimizer statistically, not bitwise, and the identical sim and QPU meshes hold for the one-circuit single/job-04 body; the iterated job-02 body returned different meshes on qpu:belenos (qd-belenos-same-meshes-drift-between-jobs).

claims.statement: On sim:belenos one 16-iteration job (32b28fe8) carries all 168 zero products and 168 bright controls of the 84 box-kite edges, certified through cd_core and mapped to 8 dark and 8 bright one-photon configurations: every dark configuration reads algebra share a = 0 (0 of 1500 one-click samples, Wilson upper bound 0.0026) and every bright one a = 1 (lower bound 0.9974) through the meshes the service re-transpiled, and the class analysis of the returned meshes reads ideal (p = 0.136).
claims.boundary: One sim:belenos job on 2026-10-18 under the simulator's default noise model; it shows the 84/84 case, the iterated mesh vehicle and the analysis reproduce the exact ideals end to end, never that hardware does.

claims.statement: On qpu:belenos the exact Q1 bright-block body, re-run after the calibration that moved the HOM figure from 92.6 % to 57.6 % with unchanged couplers, compiled to the identical circuit (sha256 9bbbaf63) and kept 0.504 (Wilson 0.494 to 0.514) of one-click samples on the block's four modes against Q1's 0.470 (0.460 to 0.480), with the leaked light again mostly on modes 17, 18 and 19; the HOM figure does not index this one-photon route's leakage.
claims.boundary: Two 10000-sample jobs on one compiled mesh, before and after one calibration; raw in-block shares only, since the receipt's dark rates that the dark-corrected figures subtract are refuted by the C1 runs (modes 0 and 1 read no clicks where they predict about 150 and 40). It says nothing about another mesh or a recalibration that changes the couplers.

claims.statement: On qpu:belenos four iterated jobs of 16 seeded uniform-random meshes each (64 settings of 1500 samples, 95,988 of the 96,000 one-click, one calibration session, all re-transpiled) read 'no class fits' under the preregistered analysis: no scanned heater-noise, gain, crosstalk or misroute magnitude reaches the fit test (median TVD 9.6 to 15.4 shot-noise floors per job), and shared static heater offsets are not declared (held-out gain about -79000 nats against fitted dephasing at the best prior width, median held-out TVD 20 floors).

It motivates a prospective test that scores a further job against these fixed efficiencies, belenos_mesh job-02 on qpu:belenos in the same coupler state.

claims.statement: Q1's single job at 10000 samples and ANU-drawn compilation_seed 46667 (job a5f0a8a4) served the fresh mesh 14a96ca6 and kept in_block 0.937 (Wilson 0.932 to 0.941), the preregistered 'mesh susceptible' reading: the single-job leak is not generic. Inside source 20's light cone D4 reads 0.990, 0.992 and 0.989: its decline is 5541 off-cone clicks, mostly on mode 5 (qd-belenos-light-cone-reading).

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 the |1> misassignment of q13 follows the state of q11 alone. With q13 alone excited (readout-q13) e10 reads 0.0456 (SE 0.0006); with q11 also excited (readout-q13-q11) 0.0913, a difference of +0.0457 at about 21 SE once q13's bracket drift between batch-00 and batch-03 (0.0019) joins the shot-noise SE in quadrature (about 45 SE on shot noise alone), established by the preregistered rule (at least 0.02 and 3 SE); with q10 excited (readout-q13-q10) 0.0396, -0.0060, and after X X on q10 and q11 that leaves both in |0> (readout-q13-xx) 0.0419, -0.0037, neither established. readout-1, with all 17 qubits excited, reads 0.0898, the q11 value. The preregistered attribution is 'state': the context dependence of q13 that the ladder established follows q11 ending in |1>. The drive control gives each neighbor two X pulses and returns it to |0>, and q10's single X raises nothing, so neither a drive effect that grows with the pulse count nor q10's single pulse explains the rise; a transient of q11's single pulse that a second pulse cancels is not separated from q11's state.
claims.boundary: One device state (17:00Z to 17:31Z, 2026-10-18), one excitation per context circuit at 131072 shots, q13 only. The q10 and drive differences are significant on shot noise alone (about 7.6 and 4.5 SE, 2.9 and 1.8 with the drift term) and below the 0.02 threshold, so they are reported, not decided. No control matches the q11 arm's single pulse with q11 returned to |0>, so a pulse-history effect of that one pulse is not excluded; the mechanism of the q11 dependence (a dispersive shift, readout-resonator crosstalk or residual coupling at measurement) is not identified, and the other block qubits' contexts were not measured.

claims.statement: The cubic Walsh exemplars (1,16) (K = 11/32, a 5-CZ circuit on three of a block's four qubits) and (9,18) (K = 5/32, 6 CZ on all four) ran on Tuna-17 blocks X = q1-q4-q8-q12 and Y = q10-q13-q11-q14 in both assignments, twice each. The preregistered decisions: the class order K_high > K_low holds on each block in both batches, the block's high-class job against its low-class job, at z 105 to 114 with the bracket drift in the SE; readout-corrected K (q13 by its neighbors' true state) reads 0.2896 and 0.2890 (high, X), 0.3050 and 0.3054 (high, Y), 0.1296 and 0.1313 (low, X), 0.1251 and 0.1252 (low, Y); the class-by-block interaction I = -0.148 (SE 0.010, a bootstrap that resamples each circuit's shots jointly over both blocks) is established, the high class doing better on Y and the low class on X; the depolarizing-shape G test rejects every job and block (log10 p -26 to -1066) under the bracket mean and under each single bracket. Replicates agree within a TVD of 0.004 to 0.008. The informational global-depolarizing prediction (0.2595 high, 0.1236 low) undershoots the high class.
claims.boundary: One device state (17:00Z to 17:31Z, 2026-10-18). The high-class circuit leaves its block's fourth qubit idle, so its forbidden outcomes measure that idle qubit alone (weight 0.003 on X, below 0.0002 on Y) and the uniform-over-16 depolarizing null is misspecified for it: the high-class shape rejection carries no information, while its K below ideal with no forbidden weight shows the noise moving weight among the eight allowed outcomes. For the same reason the interaction does not isolate a class-specific coherent error: the low class alone uses the fourth qubit and the couplers q8-q12 and q11-q14, so the classes run on different hardware subsets. The low-class shape rejection holds under all three q13 corrections and is conditional on the per-qubit readout model. The circuits test a CCZ phase polynomial under Tuna-17 noise, not composition of the sedenion multiplication blocks.

claims.statement: The hosted QX emulator (QXsinglenodesimulator, backend type 1) does not apply cQASM 3.0's measure-and-flip reset to a qubit in |1> beside a qubit in |->: reset q[0] then H on q[1] reads q[1] = 0 in 2048 of 2048 shots, where measure-and-flip reads 1 in every shot and qxelarator 0.10.0's sqrt(|a0|^2 + |a1|^2) map reads 0, while the same program with X in place of the reset and a reset of an already-zero q[0] read q[1] = 1 in 2048 of 2048. On that input the hosted reset discards q[1]'s relative phase, so a QX law of a circuit that resets a |1>-weighted qubit beside a register carrying relative phase is not the cQASM law.
claims.boundary: One batch of three two-qubit circuits on 2026-10-18 under the emulator's deployment that day. It pins the outcome of one input, a |1> reset beside one |-> qubit: it rules out measure-and-flip there and agrees with the qxelarator sqrt map, but it does not establish that map on superposed or entangled reset inputs, where another phase-dropping implementation could differ. It says nothing about Tuna hardware, whose reset is physical. A redeployed emulator can change it.

claims.statement: Over every retained qpu:belenos run of Q1's circuit, in_block over the one-click samples inside source 20's light cone of each served mesh (the modes its ideal propagation passes through, joined with every mode the exact dephasing channel at 0.5 rad heater and 0.1 rad coupler noise detects at 1e-3 or more) reads 0.982 to 0.995 in every seeded iterated cell on meshes 29dc6ef8 and 14a96ca6 at 1500 to 60000 samples and 0.985 in D3's single job on 14a96ca6, while the single jobs on 29dc6ef8 read 0.507, 0.518 (unseeded, 10000 samples), 0.918 (unseeded, 1500) and 0.370 (seed 20, 10000). Off-cone clicks sit mostly on modes 0, 1 and 5, come and go within one job on one mesh (0, 0 and 81 on identical 1500-sample iterations), and share no sample with an in-cone click in every cell but one (135 pairs where 148 are expected), where independent pulse-gated clicks predict up to 329 such pairs.

The noise-bounded cone puts at most 1.2e-4 of the photon on modes 0, 1 and 5 at an error that already halves in_block, so those clicks need a cause other than the mesh's routing; whether acquisition is pulse-gated is unknown, so their origin (photon-derived on fixed channels, or independent noise) stays open, and no single wrong source mode reproduces them. Acquisition times are estimates, samples / (physical_perf x clock), on a reading of physical_perf no Quandela document confirms. Seeded cells sit 1 to 23 shot floors from their mesh's ideal inside the cone (TVD 0.012 to 0.228), and the bridge's 22 meshes read 0.852 to 0.998 inside the ideal cone, repeating within the job; exact heater dephasing fits that spread worse than none, and static per-mesh error classes were not scanned on these meshes.

claims.statement: On qpu:belenos mesh 29dc6ef8 the requested experiment and its reported mesh fail to predict the returned output distribution of the 10000-sample single jobs, which put most of the target block on its dilation modes, where the ideal is dark: Q1 (206, 996, 1772, 1724) and (260, 1130, 1770, 1878) and job-13 (425, 1123, 849, 951) on modes 20 to 23 against the ideal (1/2, 1/2, 0, 0). The label modes hold 0.12, 0.14 and 0.15 of every one-click sample (0.26, 0.28 and 0.46 of the block) against 0.81 to 0.96 of every one-click sample in the passing Q1-circuit cells on 29dc6ef8 and 14a96ca6; a uniform survival factor leaves the normalized distribution unchanged and cannot populate a dark output. The RCA's implemented error classes over their searched ranges fit job-13 no better than TVD 0.39 against a 0.012 shot floor, the ideal outputs of the 135 complete meshes served to this account no better than 0.20 (Q1) and 0.29 (job-13), and reweighting the passing 10000-sample iteration by powers of the receipt's t_out leaves it 0.77 to 0.79 from job-13.

The record does not isolate the optical transformation from input preparation, applied settings, detector assignment, acquisition, the service's default DetectorBalancing or result assembly; the fitted phase gains (-0.30 for Q1, +0.41 for job-13) characterize the failure of one gain model, not a physical gain. The stale-load test covers only complete meshes served to this account, not a partial configuration, another account's configuration, a mixture or stale load plus further error; the reweighting test excludes the t_out family only, not arbitrary correction, mode assignment or format-dependent processing. The reported mesh hash verifies the returned circuit description, not the applied phases.

claims.statement: Q1's case on qpu:belenos at compilation_seed 20 and 10000 samples per entry, first as a ComputationIterator holding one entry (case belenos_mesh/job-14), then job-15 (a single computation, the time control) after a job-14 pass or job-16 (two identical entries) after a job-14 fail, at most two jobs and about 2.03 credits, reads each entry's in-cone TVD from the served mesh's ideal: at most 0.20 passes, at least 0.50 fails, void off 29dc6ef8 or when the result's results_list length differs from the payload sent; job-14 pass with job-15 fail reads that the failure follows the single-computation payload class.

Mitigation-off and native samples arms change the execution path and stay out. job-14 ran and failed (qd-belenos-singleton-iterator-fails-on-q1-mesh), so job-16 is the prescribed follower; a run needs the user's approval of the written case.

claims.statement: Q1's circuit sent to qpu:belenos as a ComputationIterator holding one entry at compilation_seed 20 and 10000 samples (job 3d95587b, case belenos_mesh/job-14) returned one results_list entry with one photon on mode 20 and 10000 retained samples, served Q1's mesh 29dc6ef8 and read tvd_cone_from_ideal 0.823 against a 0.004 shot floor, the preregistered fail (at least 0.50). The block read (1683, 13, 1433, 1218) on modes 20 to 23 against the ideal (1/2, 1/2, 0, 0), a label share of 0.17 of every one-click sample, with 2058 clicks on mode 19 and 1050 and 882 on modes 14 and 15: a fourth distinct wrong histogram under the same reported mesh. A one-entry iterator does not restore the behavior iterated jobs on 29dc6ef8 show (0.982 to 0.995 in-cone block retention), so the singleton iterator payload alone does not separate the failing and passing executions.
claims.boundary: One job on one mesh, about 3.2 hours after job-13. The result envelope's one entry shows the iterator representation returned, not a distinct internal worker branch. Whether a second entry, entry position or preceding execution matters is job-16's question; the service's default DetectorBalancing applied as in every earlier job.

claims.statement: In one qpu:belenos job (46b810ae, case belenos_mesh/job-16, 24 entries of Q1's circuit at 10000 samples, 149 s) the two leading seed-20 entries on 29dc6ef8 failed (tvd_cone_from_ideal 0.819 and 0.814; blocks (1708, 7, 1378, 1175) and (1788, 25, 1427, 1215) on modes 20 to 23), reproducing job-14's histogram within TVD 0.04 to 0.05, so a second entry on the same mesh does not recover; every one of the 11 following 14a96ca6 entries passed (0.080 to 0.103) and every one of the 11 29dc6ef8 entries that each followed a 14a96ca6 entry passed (0.078 to 0.104, post-load failure share 0 of 11, Wilson 95 % 0 to 0.26). The wrong state set at the start of a job on 29dc6ef8 persists while the job keeps that mesh and clears after one load of another mesh; the preregistered extension reading is '29dc6ef8 recovers after a load of another mesh while repeating the job's first mesh kept the failure'.
claims.boundary: One job, one target mesh and one reference mesh; entry order is assumed to be execution order since no result entry carries a timestamp. The failing state is reproducible within this session (job-14 and job-16 30 minutes apart) but differs from Q1's and job-13's earlier histograms, and its realized transformation matches no ideal output of the 135 meshes served to this account (best TVD 0.20) or any other source mode of 29dc6ef8 (best 0.41). Why a job that opens on 29dc6ef8 at 10000 samples fails while D2's 1500-sample opening entry on it passed, and whether a reference warm-up entry recovers other meshes or other jobs, stay open; the service's default DetectorBalancing applied throughout.

claims.statement: A proposed confirmatory cross-check of the retained exploratory coupler map uses a gate-level conditional-Ramsey case covering all 24 edges of the retained Tuna-17 coupling graph in eight induced matchings, with both probe directions, static neighbor states 0 and 1, X/Y quadratures, six identical physical delay values including zero, and full four-state joint readout calibration. The 384 Ramsey and 32 calibration circuits form 139 batches at 8192 shots each (3407872 job shots), with no CZ gates. A source-bound analyzer reconstructs omega_A, omega_B and J, checks signal quality and reciprocal-J agreement, and uses Holm correction over 24 edge tests. A separately budgeted compact QX preflight contains the same 416 circuits and 139 batches on 2 to 8 qubits at 1024 shots each (425984 emulator job shots), with fixed ideal-output criteria. Neither case has been submitted. The hardware pause ladder puts its interbatch pauses between 4140 seconds at the 30-second first step and 16560 seconds at the 120-second ceiling. It is retained as a complete offline design reference and needs a revised delay/calibration acquisition plan before submission.
claims.boundary: No acquisition or new spending authorization. Hardware batches contain at most three circuits and are acquired sequentially under the current repository policy; a compact QX preflight has its own proposed case and budget. Results would be effective static edge interactions in the declared parallel context, not reconstructed coupler flux or unique causal attribution. The Q1/Q2 nonedge and driven crosstalk require additional controls. All six delays must pass signal and phase guards; failed precision is inconclusive, not a null. Rates are conditional on the first-interval absolute range below 1 MHz, since the commensurate grid cannot identify all out-of-range aliases. The two probe directions are separate settings, not a simultaneous two-equatorial-qubit Ramsey experiment. Primitive timing sums are planning scenarios, not billed QPU time. Joint readout correction assumes assignment-channel stability across the calibration and Ramsey batches; the estimator does not remove between-batch drift. QX success would support ideal marginal gate and wiring conformance only. The retained exploratory map already found low coherence on some probes at 2 us; requiring signal at all six delays through 40 us can therefore yield inconclusive edges. Its results do not relax the prospective guards. The 139-batch version is not recommended for unchanged acquisition after the retained coherence and calibration changes; no shorter pilot is generated or authorized here. A future revision must set its own prospective thresholds rather than relax this estimator after observing data.

claims.statement: Four ibm_kingston initialization-control jobs of 100,000 shots ended in error 1305, the service's ran-longer-than timeout, with no result: at a 0 us repetition delay (inside the configuration's rep_delay_range of 0 to 2 ms, accepted by the service's range check, below the 20 us floor of IBM's changelog) both jobs stayed running for 129 s and 207 s and reported no circuit execution time, and at 20 us both jobs ended in 1305 under a 6 s execution ceiling. The service billed 2 s for each 0 us job and 5 s for each 20 us job, 14 s in all, and the settled charges match the account inventory.
claims.boundary: Code 1305 covers every ceiling cancellation in these jobs, so it does not separate a stalled shot loop from an overrun ceiling; that the 0 us jobs never started a shot loop is the inference their absent circuit execution time supports.

claims.statement: On the 149-qubit ibm_kingston initialization controls, the variance of the excited-qubit count exceeds the independent Poisson-binomial prediction by 5 to 7 percent, and the x_history excess agrees with the prep0 excess within one joint standard error at every delay (standard errors and z values from the findings document): 0.0503 against 0.0521 at 20 us, 0.0598 against 0.0594 at 50 us and 0.0623 against 0.0734 at 250 us. The excess is common to both shot histories, so it belongs to correlated readout or a common-mode event independent of the preceding shot's end state, and the independent preparation channel stands.
claims.boundary: Each history difference spans a dynamic and a static job as well as the shot history. A cell pair whose x_history excess exceeds its prep0 excess by more than the joint standard error reopens a joint preparation channel.

claims.statement: On ibm_fez the N=21 orbit loses no resolved contrast to a longer barrier-equalized feed-forward window: with the control on qubit 144 the window_delay_ramp contract fails (the doubled delay reads 0.008 above the single one), and on the pinned 083417 roles the bracketed window_delay arm reads 0.228 against the nominal 0.235. Dropping the window barriers reproduces the 083417 program and its loss, 0.094 against the bracketed 0.228 (window_overlap_loss passes, upper limit -0.110), so removing the window barriers, which lets work-qubit gates overlap the control's measure-and-reset span, costs about 59 percent of the contrast magnitude on that calibration.
claims.boundary: The run establishes the overlap cost on its calibration and attributes it to no single overlapping gate (the unbracketed arm is resynthesized, 43 CZ and 77 sx against 44 and 79); that the same overlap produced 083417's loss is the inference its identical program supports. The control-144 and control-142 assignments read different nominal magnitudes (0.151 and 0.235) under different calibrations.

claims.statement: Qubit 143 of ibm_fez loses about 37 percent of its Ramsey visibility across the 836 dt (3.3 us) orbit window with control 142 held in |0> (0.622 against 0.989 at once), and a control-state-dependent coupling accounts for at most 0.042 of it (spectator_control_zz fails, idle 0.616 against idle_ground 0.622). The grounded delay sweep reads visibility 0.997, 0.612, 0.395, 0.885, 0.743, 0.255 and 0.705 at 0 to 20.064 us in 3.344 us steps: the preregistered decay_shape test reads neither, the visibilities are non-monotone, and the T2* of 7 us drawn from two points is withdrawn.
claims.boundary: The preregistered shape and detuning fits describe no identified parameter (the stretch exponent sits on its bound and the single-frequency model is contradicted). The two-component fit (beat-model.json static model: a = 0.644, envelope 135.6 us) is descriptive and post hoc, and the non-monotone revivals it describes reject no monotone model through a registered decision; its splitting aliases at the 3.344 us sampling, and charge-parity splitting against a two-level-system coupling is undecided; a dense 0.25 us sweep resolves both.

claims.statement: In the segmented coprime sweep of ibm_fez qubit 143 (48 PUBs x 1536 shots, six segments per shot, every member admitted on its returned schedule and heralds), the two lines are a classical mixture fixed within each shot: an exchange-coupled two-level system fits worse by 10063 in NLL, the Z arms carry no swap memory (18.3 against 42.3) and the 1250 dt herald pre-idle moves no quadrature (3.5 against 13.7). The splitting df = -90.2 kHz lies in alias cell 0, resolved by 5350 in NLL over the next cell, with weights 0.529 / 0.471. In shot order the line labels of the half-cycle delays correlate across columns 8.934 ms apart (the metered circuit execution time per shot) and decay as a two-state telegraph with switching time tau = 26.2 ms (moving-block bootstrap 2.5 to 97.5 percent 19.3 to 30.5 ms; dwell 56 and 50 ms; 28.3 ms at the chunk's wall period, an upper bound). The raw reads of the four whole-cycle delays up to 30.5 us correlate within 0.034 at lag 1 (standard error 0.026); at 8316 dt the raw correlation 0.090 equals that arm's own label correlation 0.089, the residual line separation at 33 us.
claims.boundary: The preregistered segmented-sweep.json refuses every member (the bound reader kept a barrier before INIT on the ibm_fez table); the verdicts come from the amended analyzer at closure 759d82d74c57 (correcting closure 6d59d710eb61's unconverged fits) and the switching time from a post hoc shot-order analysis, so neither confirms. The near-equal weights fixed over a shot fit charge-parity splitting, which a parity-resolved readout would test; a dispersively coupled two-level fluctuator switching in tens of ms predicts the same telegraph. Shot-to-shot correlation at 9.7 ms makes the per-shot Wald statistics anti-conservative; the non-rejections and the model and alias margins survive that.

claims.statement: The same segmented sweep on ibm_marrakesh qubit 47, a qubit with no recorded beat, admits every member and reads exchangeable segments (51.5 against 72.1), herald backaction (47.9 against 13.7) and Z memory (284 against 42.3), with a 0.105 second line at alias cell 0 (df -12.9 kHz, the next cell worse by 317 in NLL), T1 81 us and T2* 60 us from the static fit.
claims.boundary: The owner approved moving the run to ibm_kingston or ibm_marrakesh before it was submitted, while ibm_fez held over 1,400 pending jobs, and the Marrakesh dry run pinned qubit 47 in place of 143; its alias lattice and priors come from qubit 143, so the second line and its cell read a weak structure through another qubit's priors. The verdicts come from the amended analyzer at closure 759d82d74c57, whose preconditioned fit corrects closure 6d59d710eb61's cell -2 and T2* 52 us (decay times left at their starts).

claims.statement: The Tuna-17 order pilot completed 24 jobs and 393216 shots. Six native-zero dark-port controls measured 0.0396118 to 0.0508423; two native-0.25 settings measured 0.2669067 and 0.2703857. The refreshed ledger records 186.801814 execution seconds and zero credit debit.
claims.boundary: One fixed chronological acquisition per science setting leaves preparation, compiled-circuit effects, readout and time drift confounded. The observations establish neither representative equivalence, process fidelity, calibrated uncertainty coverage nor a fundamental quaternion scalar field.
assumptions: Provider shot order is retained as delivered; timing and stationarity are unestablished.

claims.statement: The registered finite exact calculations give derivation dimension 14, chosen-octonion stabilizer dimension 8, occupation dimensions 1/3/3/1 and complex Clifford image dimension 64. The draft ladder pairing fails six stabilizer checks, while the aligned pairing passes all implemented checks. The even five-mode reference has vanishing recorded Standard Model anomaly sums.
claims.boundary: Finite convention-bound algebra and a representation reference establish neither a unique Standard Model derivation nor its dynamics, a fundamental scalar field, or device performance.
assumptions: The registered cd_core multiplication convention and explicit encoding maps fix the finite basis calculations.

claims.statement: The first eight canonical sedenion left-multiplication operators satisfy the recorded Cl(0,8) relations. Their 256 integer word operators have Hilbert-Schmidt Gram matrix 16 times identity and span M16(R).
claims.boundary: The result concerns the named eight-generator associative operator envelope. Sedenion coefficient multiplication remains nonassociative with zero divisors; the left encoding is not a product homomorphism.
assumptions: The registered cd_core multiplication convention and explicit encoding maps fix the finite basis calculations.

claims.statement: The frozen BDSC qualification job tc-*-e1 (12 iterations of the 77-parameter ladder-union circuit, 300000 samples each, QRNG seeds) ran end to end on sim:belenos under both policies: the empty-list job 19f18f8c in 148 s and the provider-default rerun cac942bd in 153 s, 1 credit each. Every iteration returned its 300000 samples with its circuit_params bit-exact and its compilation_seed echoed; f read 0 and g read 1 under both templates, the eight superposition states read 0.4989 to 0.5017 against 0.5, and the one-click rule excluded at most 21 samples per iteration. The first provider-default job 03dd195b stopped at iteration 4 (55 s of compute, progress 0.2567, progress message probs) and ended in Worker timeout after about 30 minutes without charge; the identical rerun completed.
claims.boundary: Simulator runs only; sim:belenos applies a fixed noise model and its default DetectorBalancing returns counts drawn from a corrected distribution, so neither policy here tests the QPU's observation contract, and the readout admits qpu:belenos runs only. One timeout in two provider-default runs establishes no rate; Perceval computes the same noisy distribution in 0.1 s locally, so the stall is placed in the service worker by inference.

claims.statement: While qpu:belenos read running on its Explorer row and processor record, then calibration, a one-computation job (90712931, box_kite_photonic_single job-00, 10000 samples) entered the token's queue and stayed waiting with no start time for 26 minutes; it was canceled with 0 shots and no charge (qpu:belenos usage 17.2255 before and after). The run retains no read of the public platform list in that interval, so the observation concerns the Explorer and processor status only.
claims.boundary: One job in one window; whether running ever admits a job, and how long such a window lasts, is not measured.

claims.statement: In epoch 1 of the frozen BDSC qualification case on qpu:belenos (jobs 2524f061, b5bdf7f2, 2bc57917, 6d2dac12; 48 settings, 300000 samples each, every iteration's parameters and seed echoed, at most 0.06 % excluded by the one-click rule, 1.6 credits per job) the within-cell sum rules p(+) + p(-) = p(f) + p(g) read 9 violated, 4 inconclusive and 3 compatible of 16 at margin 0.02 on the case's simultaneous Clopper-Pearson event restricted to epoch 1. Under the empty mitigation list the target-complement pair reads f 0.002 to 0.004 and g 0.986 against ideal 0 and 1 while all eight superposition states read 0.375 to 0.437 against 0.5; the cross-template contrasts read 13 compatible, 5 violated and 6 inconclusive of 24. Only the empty-list job returned zero-click outcomes (25 to 140 per iteration), so the provider-default route processes what it returns.
claims.boundary: Epoch 1 alone, read before the frozen readout: the case decides only on all 96 observations across both epochs, and admission waits on the provider-contract answers, so this is no qualification verdict. A violated sum rule says the prepared states differ from the requested ones for any fixed effect; attributing it to the compiled mesh's phases rather than the detection stage is an inference the design does not isolate.

claims.statement: A 12-iteration template job on qpu:ascella (c2edef5d, 2026-10-21 20:34 UTC, platform reading available) ended in error 1 s after starting with failure_code RUNTIME ERROR and 'hardware_info.circuit_input_ports must be defined in the hardware_config to use Instruments.set_pic_input()', its one results_list entry, for the first of the 12 iterations (seed 0), holding that text instead of counts and the other eleven iterations returning no entry; it was charged nothing (qpu:ascella 0.0 credits for 1 job).
