claims.statement: The repeat acquisition of the target-complement state pair under Quandela's default mitigation on qpu:belenos (job ee6fc975, case job tc-def-e2; submitted 2026-10-22 01:35 UTC under platform status running, started after a 42-minute queue wait, ran 92 s, 1.6 credits) returned all 12 settings at 300000 samples with at most 0.032 % excluded by the one-click rule, and the freshly built job body carried the requested policy, so the submission and collection path at collector revision f1dc1c0 works end to end. Against the first acquisition of the same job (2524f061, 2026-10-21) the basis states f and g moved by at most 0.0033 while the eight superposition states moved by -0.071 to +0.041, many times the binomial standard error of about 0.001, and the within-template sum-rule residuals p(+) + p(-) - p(f) - p(g) read -0.080 and -0.039 (outward ladder, real and imaginary pairs) and -0.032 and -0.081 (reverse ladder) against -0.035, +0.031, -0.042 and +0.000 in the first acquisition. Between the two acquisitions the published source figures moved from HOM 87.3 to 87.8 % to 80.4 %, transmittance 6.05 to 6.13 % to 5.25 % and g2 1.0 % to 0.9 %.
claims.boundary: One repeat job, run as the engineering validation of the runbook's first 2026-10-22 amendment (step 5). scripts/bdsc_cases.py draws each compilation seed by observation index, epoch included, so all 12 settings ran with new seeds and returned different circuits: the shift compares matched requests, not matched compilations. The forensic reading (docs/notes/quandela/bdsc-acceptance-diagnostics.md, rated moderate) takes the 0.035 spread of the superpositions about their common drop as a per-compilation response and leaves the common drop of 0.024 unsplit between the device, its characterization and the default policy's processing. No calibration cycle between the two acquisitions is documented, so the shift supports no claim about reproducibility across a recalibration. The residuals are point differences without a simultaneous interval; the crossed diagnostic case, which replaces the suspended confirmation design, is the design that separates these components.

claims.statement: The hosted QX emulator returned the preregistered exact outcomes of all 41 BDSC Pauli readout circuits of the twin series (14 batches, 2048 shots each, completed 2026-10-22 10:35 to 10:41 UTC, 0 credits): every kernel+bright-1 pair residual and middle or sector residual is within its preregistered bound, and the matched quadrature phase is 0.0039, 0.0029 and -0.0181 rad (standard error 0.0156) on the three patches, consistent with zero. The control verdict passes with no miss, so each Tuna-17 patch's gate sequence, which the case builder requires the twin to repeat on relabeled qubits, is semantically clean before it reaches Tuna-17.
claims.boundary: Noiseless emulator semantics of the twin's 10-qubit circuits, which pack two relabeled patches each; the 17-qubit Tuna-17 files, their physical qubit indices and their three-patch composition are not executed by this control, and it carries no device noise, readout or calibration behavior. The retained analysis was written by the Quantum Inspire interpreter and is bound by sha256 in every Tuna-17 series-gate.json, so its replay accepts float rounding within 1e-12 relative.

claims.statement: The preregistered Tuna-17 pilot of the BDSC target effect (27 circuits in 9 batches of 3, 32768 shots each, all completed, 540.8 s of execution, 0 credits, created 2026-10-22 10:42 UTC and finished 11:49 UTC) ended with its bracket drift stop fired: the readout-1 reference's P(0|1) on qubit 1 moved from 0.0735 in batch 06 to 0.0453 in batch 08, a change of 0.0283 against the 0.02 stop. The batch-00 assignment stop stayed clear, and the drift between consecutive references stayed at or below 0.0187 through batch 07. Under the preregistered rule a fired stop withholds every score, pair chi-square, phase and mitigated estimate, so the series makes no endpoint decision.
claims.boundary: The registered decision is the stop itself. The backend reported calibrating at 11:32 UTC, between batches 06 and 08, which fits a recalibration as the cause of the drift but is not established by any retained probe. No witness score, branch phase or device qualification follows from these acquisitions, and nothing here bears on any Belenos measurement.

claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (station control 50.0.0, calibration set 9069c4ef), two jobs of X and a bare measure on QB1 at 2000 shots each billed ceil(runtime), not ceil(the compiler's execution runtime estimate): 2 s for a 1.306 s runtime under passive reset and 1 s for 0.205 s under active_reset_cycles 1, against estimates of 2.804 s and 1.617 s, 1.50 credits in all. The estimates follow 1.60 s per job plus each shot's schedule within 0.02 s. Execution took 316 us per shot under passive reset and 37.5 us under active reset. Active reset left the bare measure at P(1) 0.0680 against 0.0065 under passive reset (difference 0.0615, z 10.4), so one active-reset cycle does not keep QB1's initialization. The passive job read X at 0.9705 and the bare measure at 0.0065, within three standard errors of the calibration-built predictions 0.9817 and 0.0046 (z -2.96 and +1.06).
claims.boundary: One qubit (QB1), one calibration set and one active-reset setting (one cycle); billing is the service's rule on 2026-10-22. The excess bare-measure P(1) under active reset is not separated into residual excitation and reset-induced readout error. The H4 bare-measure prediction in the design document was the simulator's 2000-shot sample 0.003; the decision uses the exact unheralded P(1|0) 0.0046. The garnet:mock jobs fix the estimate model only; their measurement data are random bits.

claims.statement: The garnet:mock pipeline estimated 2.007 s for one circuit of 1000 shots, 3.227 s for one circuit of 4000 shots and for twenty circuits of 200 shots, and 1.635 s for 4000 shots with active_reset_cycles 1: a fixed 1.60 s per job plus 0.407 ms per passive-reset shot (the mock calibration's 400 us reset_wait, 1.2 us readout and 5 us end delay), no cost per extra circuit, and about 9 us per active-reset shot. Each job charged 0.00 credits, and the mock returned random bits (P(1) 0.48 to 0.51 for an X).
claims.boundary: Mock estimates under the mock's own calibration; the hardware estimate, runtime and billing are the reset and billing pilot's.

claims.statement: The garnet:mock pipeline accepted both jobs of the signed kernel probe case (cases.json dd9cdf84) with heralding_mode zeros and active_reset_cycles 1, estimated 3.05 s for 2 circuits x 20000 shots and 8.86 s for 10 circuits x 20000, charged 0.00 credits, and returned 4918 to 5068 shots per circuit: the server returns only the heralded shots and does not top up the request.
claims.boundary: The mock's bits are random, so its kept fraction says nothing about Garnet's heralding retention.

claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (calibration set 9069c4ef, 199 CZ on QB6, QB7, QB10, QB11, QB12, QB16 and QB17, one active-reset cycle with all-zeros heralding keeping 55.9 % of shots), the structure-matched signed probe of the certified sedenion kernel u = (e4 - e15)/sqrt2 of L(e1+e10) read the odd part (Z(t) - Z(-t))/2 of its control at +0.0220 +- 0.0067 for |t| = 0.25 (z 3.29, the sign of t resolved) and +0.0058 +- 0.0030 for |t| = 0.05 (z 1.94, unresolved), so the dilation overlap Re<v|B(t)|u> = t/(2 + |t|) is not falsified and the device carries its sign at |t| = 0.25. Both odd parts fit one visibility, V = 0.206 +- 0.054 times t/(2 + |t|) (chi-square 0.08, 1 dof), and the even offsets read -0.022 and -0.012. The jobs charged 4.50 credits.
claims.boundary: One compile, one calibration set and two values of |t|; the |t| = 0.05 arm is underpowered, not a confirmation. The calibration-built simulator (depolarizing gates, readout errors, ALAP idle T1/T2) predicted odd parts +0.0296 and +0.0188 and even offsets near +0.029: the small-|t| odd part and the sign of the offsets depart from it, so its non-unital relaxation term does not describe this device. Heralding removes the active-reset excitation measured by iqm-garnet-reset-billing-pilot; it does not test the dark-probe law t^2/(2 + |t|)^2. The signed overlap equals t/(2 + |t|) for every unit vector u (signed-overlap-kernel-independence), so the run establishes that Garnet carries a relative pi phase on the signed branch through this compile, not a property of the sedenion kernel. Coherent gate errors add an odd term proportional to sqrt(|t|/(2 + |t|)) (iqm-garnet-signed-probe-coherent-response), so the single-visibility fit does not separate the linear law from that term: the measured ratio odd(0.05)/odd(0.25) = 0.26 +- 0.16 lies between the linear 0.22 and the amplitude scaling 0.47. The strong job lists its +t circuit before its -t circuit and the weak job its five +t circuits before its five -t circuits, so a reading that depends on batch position enters the odd part: a device with no signed response and a -0.044 shift on the second circuit reproduces the strong arm's +0.022, and the sign at |t| = 0.25 is resolved only under the assumption that position does not move the reading.

claims.statement: In the sedenions (cd_core) the signed dilation overlap <L_e2 u|(L_e1 + L_e10 + t L_e2) u>/(2 + |t|) equals t/(2 + |t|) for every real unit vector u, in the kernel of L(e1 + e10) or not, because L_e2 is orthogonal and L_e2^T L_e1 and L_e2^T L_e10 are antisymmetric (exact integer identities); as checks, the certified kernel vector (e4 - e15)/sqrt2, the bright vector (e4 + e15)/sqrt2, e4 and a seeded random vector all read it, and on the kernel support {e4, e15} all 1000 seeded replacement sign tables leave it unchanged. The zero-divisor property is instead the eigenvalue -1 of K = L_e1^T L_e10 on u (K swaps e4 and e15, and its -1 eigenspace is four-dimensional): the cancellation observable cos^2(theta) <w|L_e1 u> + sin^2(theta) <w|L_e10 u> with w = L_e1 u reads cos(2 theta) for the kernel vector and 1 for the bright vector, and one flipped L_e10 sign at e4 or e15, or 755 of the 1000 sign tables, removes its zero at theta = pi/4.
claims.boundary: Exact arithmetic over the listed vectors and the seeded sign tables; it says nothing about a device, and a hardware reading of the cancellation observable needs its own approved case.

claims.statement: For Cayley-Dickson dimension 2^n, n = 1 to 6 (cd_core), the sign f(p, q) in e_p e_q = (-1)^f(p, q) e_(p xor q) has algebraic normal form degree max(2, n) over the 2n index bits, with C(n, 2) + n monomials of degree 2 and (2^(k - 1) - 1) C(n, k) of degree k >= 3, and degree max(1, n - 1) in q maximized over the left factor p, which Theorem 1 of docs/notes/cd_phase_degree.md proves for every n (n - 1 for every nonzero p, n >= 2); the joint degree and the monomial counts are this certificate's addition. Octonion left multiplication is therefore at most a degree-2 phase, implementable with CZ and Z gates, and sedenion left multiplication reaches a degree-3 phase.
claims.boundary: Enumerated for n <= 6; the closed form beyond n = 6 is a conjecture this certificate does not prove. Degree bounds the order of the multi-controlled phases a sign diagonal needs, not the routed CZ count on a lattice.

claims.statement: On the retained Garnet compile of the signed kernel probe (transpiler seed 2, 199 CZ on seven qubits), the first-order response of the measured <Z> on QB7 to coherent gate errors (prx over-rotation and axis error per qubit, residual Z after each CZ per qubit, CZ conditional phase per coupler) vanishes in the odd part at t = 0 for every error and grows with the signed amplitude sqrt(|t|/(2 + |t|)), not with t: the QB6 over-rotation coefficient per unit amplitude is -7.1, -6.9 and -6.2 at |t| = 0.01, 0.05 and 0.25. The even part responds at first order, led by QB11 over-rotation (-8.0 per unit relative over-rotation at |t| = 0.05), residual Z on QB11 (-1.56) and QB12 over-rotation (+1.15), Through the calibration noise model (exact density-matrix probabilities, each error inserted after scheduling) every response shrinks to 5 to 10 % of its noiseless size, unevenly (QB11 over-rotation -0.43, QB12 over-rotation +0.002): QB11 alone would need a 10.5 % over-rotation, three times the 3.5 % its randomized-benchmarking infidelity allows, and all 29 terms aligned at that bound move the even part by at most 0.032, short of the measured circuit-level -0.045.
claims.boundary: First-order derivatives of the compiled circuit, noiseless and through the calibration noise model, under a stationary error model (one relative over-rotation and one axis error per qubit, one residual Z per qubit after CZ, one conditional phase per coupler); angle-dependent, time-dependent and crosstalk errors and leakage lie outside it, and the noisy derivatives inherit the calibration model, whose even part the device contradicts. The device's coherent error magnitudes are unmeasured.

claims.statement: The first three qpu:belenos submissions of block 1 of the approved crossed BDSC diagnostic (job 5aec4d50 submitted 2026-10-22 11:06:58 UTC; e51b9f4f submitted 11:15:53; e51b9f4f's resubmission 2d868daa submitted 11:17:33) each ended canceled with 0 shots, no start time and status message 'Cancel requested from perceval', and qpu:belenos usage held at 25.2255 free credits in every usage report the receipts retain. The two later submissions departed from the frozen protocol: the first job's collection at 11:15:35 already met the case's stop conditions (fewer than 40000 samples, no compiled circuit), which end the four-job sequence. None of the three runs enters the diagnostic readout; block 1 was rerun from its first job under the owner's fresh approval, 'jobs approved.', given after this record was reported.
claims.boundary: An operational record: no device measurement, setting response or statement about Belenos availability follows from these runs. The service records only that a client requested each cancel; which client sent it is outside the retained evidence.

claims.statement: Block 1 of the approved crossed BDSC diagnostic on qpu:belenos completed: job c8d90a80 (submitted 2026-10-22 16:00:38 UTC) and job ef06045d (submitted 16:03:56 UTC, started after job 1 ended) each returned all 24 iterations with 960000 samples in total and 164 s of execution, with no partial result. Block 2 and the readout follow under the same approval; the preregistered readout over all four jobs carries the diagnostic's inference.

claims.statement: The first submission of block 2 job 1 (4058ce4e, created 2026-10-22 17:09 UTC) held 0 shots with no start time until its collection at 00:46 UTC on 2026-10-23, 7.6 hours later, which recorded status canceled, 0 shots and status message 'Cancel requested from perceval'. Its resubmission (a5a0d2cf) and block 2 job 2 (33499aec) each returned all 24 iterations with 960000 samples in 164 s and 171 s, and block 2 job 2 was submitted at 08:13:30 UTC, 25 s after block 2 job 1's collection; no receipt of the matched check from that interval is retained, and --matched-check reproduces the equality of block 2 job 1's returned circuits with block 1 job 2's on the retained runs.
claims.boundary: An operational record of one canceled and two completed jobs. The resubmission continued past a stop condition of the frozen case with no amendment retained before it (the runbook's protocol deviation of 2026-10-23), so the readout over the four completed jobs is descriptive.

claims.statement: The readout of the four completed jobs, by the preregistered rule, of the crossed BDSC diagnostic on qpu:belenos (96 instances: six target-complement states x two templates x four QRNG seeds x two blocks, 40000 samples per iteration with 39959 to 40000 eligible one-click trials, empty mitigation) selects the stationarity branch: matched requests changed between the blocks beyond their class means (heterogeneity statistic 553 on 45 degrees of freedom) while all 48 matched pairs returned identical compiled circuits and no instance leaked. Outside the branch rule, the support-conditioned rerun finds the matched changes homogeneous about their class means (45.8 on 45), so the instance-specific change lives in the aggregate fraction of clicks outside each setting's target support, while the superpositions keep a common on-support shift of -0.0048 (z -7.7); the g basis state shifted by +0.0035 (z 11.6); the seed effect on the superpositions is state-specific in both readings and stays so among seed slots that share a job (2406 on 24 raw, 1941 on 24 support-conditioned); and all 32 sum-rule residuals lie beyond the 0.02 margin, between -0.14 and -0.24.
claims.boundary: One device, two blocks a day apart, read descriptively: block 2 was resubmitted past a stop condition with no amendment retained before it (the runbook's protocol deviation of 2026-10-23). Standard errors and p-values are reference values under independent Bernoulli trials, uncalibrated while the provider contract leaves count provenance and uncorrected observations unresolved. Identical returned circuits show one nominal model; attributing the change to the device rather than the compiler holds only if a returned circuit describes the configuration that ran, which the contract leaves unresolved. The branch names the next amendment, stationarity and provider calibration before any fixed-effect confirmation, which reruns under that amendment; it makes no certification decision, and physical_perf ratios stay an uninterpreted provider diagnostic.

claims.statement: Vetoing output mode 5, which lies outside every selection and target support of the crossed BDSC diagnostic on qpu:belenos and whose plan-time dark-count rate in every run receipt (3137.7 per second before block 1, 1847.5 before block 2) is the largest of any mode, removes the instance-specific block change of the four completed diagnostic jobs: the heterogeneity of matched requests about their class means falls from 553 to 58.0 on 45 degrees of freedom (p 0.09) whether the mode-5 one-click samples leave the eligible count or the mode-5 detector is removed from every pattern. Across the 48 matched instances the mode-5 share changed by -0.0069 with standard deviation 0.0119, while every other off-support mode together changed by +0.0002 with standard deviation 0.0026. Under the veto the g basis state's block shift reads -0.0007 (z -3.6) instead of +0.0035, the superpositions keep a common shift of -0.0044 (z -7.2), the seed effects stay resolved, and the mode-5 share falls with position in two of the four jobs (rank correlation -0.49 and -0.47, p 0.016 and 0.020). The block-mean mode-5 share fell from 0.0144 to 0.0075, a ratio of 0.52 against the plan-time dark-rate ratio of 0.59, and the coincident trials (one mode-5 click beside exactly one other click) carry the same selected fraction as the other eligible trials (47.7 over 66 instances, conditional hypergeometric p 0.40).
claims.boundary: The veto was chosen after the diagnostic's outcomes were seen, on runs that are themselves read descriptively (the runbook's protocol deviation of 2026-10-23), so it names a hypothesis that the stationarity amendment of the qualification runbook tests on new data and confirms nothing. Standard errors are reference values under independent Bernoulli trials. The dark-count rate is a plan-time platform reading, not an acquisition-time measurement: the two block-1 jobs share one reading yet their mean mode-5 shares differ (0.0123 and 0.0165), and physical_perf supplies no confirmed acquisition clock (docs/notes/quandela/strategy.md), so the ranks of the share against dark rate / physical_perf are a conditional diagnostic and the dark-click mechanism stays a candidate.

claims.statement: garnet:mock refused the kernel cancellation job while Garnet's calibration set 9069c4ef was pinned for every quantum computer ('Calibration set not found', 0.00 credits); with the set pinned for Garnet alone it accepted all 21 circuits (37-CZ probe arms, readout calibration and 1- to 41-pulse prx trains) under heralding_mode zeros and one active-reset cycle, compiled against its own set f04fe114, estimated 2.80 s for 21 circuits x 4000 shots and charged 0.00 credits. The case rebuilt on Garnet's live set 68b0f1d0 (25 circuits, cases.json f8c814d1) ran on garnet:mock with an estimate of 3.01 s and 0.00 credits, and its 27-circuit successors with a readout calibration for every measured qubit (cases.json b3a9e166, then 19407dd2 with exact predictions bound into cases.json) with 3.09 s and 0.00 credits each.
claims.boundary: The mock's bits are random, so the run tests acceptance, schema and the runtime estimate, not the probe's physics; it does not show whether the server plays consecutive prx pulses separately.

claims.statement: On Garnet the kernel cancellation probe (37 CZ on QB6, QB7, QB11, QB12 and QB17, calibration set 68b0f1d0) reads the control's <Z> as -V sin(2 phi) for the certified sedenion kernel vector around the balanced selector theta = pi/4 + phi and as V for the bright vector (e4 + e15)/sqrt2, so the odd part at phi = 0.1 and 0.3 carries the zero-divisor sign (the eigenvalue -1 of L_e1^T L_e10) while the bright odd part stays zero. The calibration model (exact, herald-conditioned readout) predicts visibility 0.48, kernel odd parts -0.0945 and -0.269, and a kernel even part of +0.052 from idle relaxation and readout; QB11's over-rotation, measured by prx trains of 1 to 13 pulses in the same job and fitted as -sin(N pi/2 eps), adds the noise model's -0.75 eps to that even part. Falsifiers: a kernel odd part three standard errors above zero (H1), a bright odd part three from the modeled bright odd part of idle relaxation (H2), the contrast odd(0.3) - (sin(0.6)/sin(0.2)) odd(0.1) three from zero (H3), the kernel even part three from its decomposition (H4); both kernel contrasts list their arms +, -, -, +.
claims.boundary: cd_core settles the zero-divisor property exactly, so a resolved H1 demonstrates that the device realizes the compiled sign table at first order rather than discovering an algebraic fact; the open questions are device physics (QB11's coherent error, the even-part decomposition, the response shape). No approved hardware case; the prediction carries no coherent error, and H4 rests on the model's relaxation even part and on QB11's over-rotation being the only first-order term of this compile under the audit's stationary error model; an angle-dependent QB11 error rescales the odd part by twice what its trains predict and leaves its sign.

claims.statement: garnet:mock accepted both jobs of the signed kernel null re-test (16 heralded 199-CZ circuits x 20000 shots and 10 readout and prx-train circuits x 4000), estimated 13.2 s and 2.04 s, and charged 0.00 credits, both before and after cases.json bound its exact prediction (cases.json ece7a3f2).

claims.statement: On Garnet (calibration set 68b0f1d0, the retained 199-CZ compile) the null-controlled re-test reads D(0.25) = odd(0.25) - odd(0) over two +, -, -, + blocks at |t| = 0.25 and at t = 0: the retained +0.022 at |t| = 0.25 carries the sign of t only if D(0.25) lies three standard errors above zero. The calibration model (exact, herald-conditioned readout) predicts an odd part of +0.0136 at t = 0 and D(0.25) = +0.0095 (+0.0059 with a 2.7 % QB11 over-rotation), so a model-like device leaves D(0.25) unresolved at the planned standard error of 0.0047, while the retained visibility of 0.206 puts it near 4.8 standard errors. A |t| = 0.05 resolve sized at that visibility took 16 blocks (ceiling 43.5 credits); at the visibility the re-test then measured (0.058) it needs about 202 blocks and is not built.
claims.boundary: No approved hardware case; the observable is kernel-independent (signed-overlap-kernel-independence), so the re-test measures the device's carried phase and its null offset, not the sedenion kernel.

claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (calibration set 68b0f1d0, the retained 199-CZ compile of the signed kernel probe, two +, -, -, + blocks at |t| = 0.25 and at t = 0, 20000 shots each, heralding keeping 50263 to 50591 shots per arm), the odd part (Z(t) - Z(-t))/2 of QB7 read +0.0090 +- 0.0031 at |t| = 0.25 and +0.0025 +- 0.0031 at t = 0 (copies weighted equally), so D(0.25) = odd(0.25) - odd(0) = +0.0065 +- 0.0045 (z 1.46): unresolved under the preregistered three-standard-error decision. The visibility after the null subtraction is 0.058, inside the calibration model's 0.05 to 0.09 and a quarter of the 0.206 the original run implied; the even part read -0.0175 and -0.0195, reproducing the original run's negative offsets. The jobs charged 5.50 credits.
claims.boundary: One calibration set. The observable is kernel-independent (signed-overlap-kernel-independence), so the re-test bounds the device's carried phase, not the sedenion kernel. The original run's +0.022 at |t| = 0.25 lies 1.8 standard errors (their combined error) above this run's +0.0090 at the same |t|; with that run's +t before -t order and no t = 0 arm, a batch-position effect, the null offset and a fluctuation are not separated.

claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (calibration set be070414, job 01a175ac-da6c-718e-8efc-438c1bff1c46, 57 circuits x 3000 shots, 5.00 credits, QB1, QB5, QB8, QB14, QB17, QB19) the preregistered departure test of ideal pinching reads none: departs_below and exceeds_prediction both read none at pooled z +1.65, with all six qubits informative (mutation z 36 to 56; the N = 16 measure-minus-unitary contrast 0.80 to 0.83 against the ideal 0.861). The measure arm's N = 16 P0 sits 0.022 to 0.042 above its prediction on every qubit (0.5 to 0.85 standard errors at the departure standard error of 0.044 to 0.049, which carries a gate-model systematic floored at 0.04). By the reach fixed before the data, the none bounds the measurement to a transition probability below about 0.006 per measurement, or to less than about 30 % of the coherence surviving each measurement.
claims.boundary: Exploratory. The reach is set by the gate-model floor of 0.04 in P0, not by the shot count, and no tighter bound follows from this run. The unitary arm departs from its model by -0.028 (QB14, statistical z -5.4), -0.026 (QB1) and -0.018 (QB5), beyond 3 statistical standard errors on three qubits, which the widened standard error absorbs. The eps fits to P0(N) have chi-square 58 to 196 on 4 degrees of freedom with negative eps, so the single-transition-loss description fails. Four qubits fit a negative initialization excitation (down to -0.067), which the readout model reads through q and does not separate from a thermal excitation of the idle qubit. The preregistered gate-model systematic evaluated the axis-phase class on the +1 signed circuit only, while the experiment pools the circuits +, -, -, +; the sign-pooled reanalysis (results/iqm/measurement_sequence_pinching_sign_pooled_analysis.json, gate core-710) has an axis-phase ratio of -0.017 to -0.018 against +0.31 to +0.35 one-sign, gate systematics of 0.040 to 0.046 against 0.042 to 0.048, departure standard errors of 0.042 to 0.047 against 0.044 to 0.049, and a pooled departure z of +1.72 against +1.65. The verdict is unchanged: both read none, and the reach (a transition probability below about 0.006 per measurement, or less than about 30 % coherence surviving each measurement) is unchanged at that precision: with the injection scale and the analysis both sign-pooled the smallest detectable shifts are 0.047 to 0.070 in P0 (eps 0.0040 to 0.0061), against 0.049 to 0.073 (0.0042 to 0.0064) preregistered.

claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (calibration set be070414, job 01a175ac-da6c-718e-8efc-438c1bff1c46, 3000 shots, QB1, QB5, QB8, QB14, QB17, QB19) the preregistered settle-tail rule reads attributed at pooled z +4.81, by the count rule on QB14 (+3.15) and QB5 (+3.43). The rule compares the settle arm's N = 16 P0, which adds a 2.0 us idle after each mid-circuit measure to the measure arm, with the model's prediction from the measure arm's own N = 16 loss and the in-job T1: lengthening the post-measurement idle from zero to 2 us raised P0 beyond that prediction by +0.0066 (QB1), +0.0161 (QB5), +0.0056 (QB8), +0.0156 (QB14) and +0.0125 (QB17) and lowered it by 0.0056 on QB19.
claims.boundary: Exploratory observation without a mechanism. The effect may come from a readout tail or from measurement-induced relaxation during the idle, and a tail slower than 2 us stays unexcluded. The tail gap carries its delta-method standard error with no gate-model floor; the settle and measure arms play identical pulses. The preregistration text was inconsistent about the settle arm (conditioned on a departure, decides nothing, or feeds the device verdict); the reported attributed comes from the code's unconditional per-qubit and device rule, and no qubit departs in this run, so under the conditional reading the gap would be descriptive only.

claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (calibration set a18a947f, 24 circuits x 4500 shots, one active-reset cycle, no heralding), a circuit job runs its gates as soon as possible: in both idle layouts every qubit uncoupled to the train qubit (QB1, then QB20), pulsed once beside 500 or 1000 identity pi pulses and read in one joint measure, relaxed toward |0>, and all 68 pulsed-qubit arms resolved ASAP against the ALAP prediction of no change, at 13.3 to 58.7 standard errors from the midpoint of the two predictions (H1). Fitted with its own readout pair, QB11's isolated prx train reads a relative over-rotation of -0.30 +- 0.06 %, which excludes the +2.7 % the null-controlled signed probe's prediction attributes to it at 47 standard errors, and QB6's reads -0.18 +- 0.07 % (H2; chi-square 8.1 and 1.2 on three degrees of freedom). The job ran 1.92 s, billed 2 s and charged 1.00 credit.
claims.boundary: One calibration set and one job. The decay is larger than the ASAP model predicts (observed over predicted contrast 0.86 to 2.39, median 1.63; apparent T1 at 1000 pulses 0.40 to 1.27 of the calibrated value, median 0.53), so the model's 16 ns per prx, the calibrated T1, or both understate the wait; that is unresolved here and decides nothing. The parallel block's fits are descriptive: 13 of 20 qubits fit the linear train model, and QB2, QB5, QB7, QB11, QB15, QB16 and QB17 do not when all qubits are driven at once; QB6 reads -0.22 +- 0.10 % parallel minus isolated. Retained predictions keep the ALAP schedule their approvals covered.

claims.statement: On IQM Garnet (calibration set 68b0f1d0, 37 CZ on QB6, QB7, QB11, QB12 and QB17, one active-reset cycle with all-zeros heralding), the kernel cancellation probe read the control's odd part (Z(phi) - Z(-phi))/2 at -0.0699 +- 0.0087 for phi = 0.1 (z -8.0) and -0.178 +- 0.009 for phi = 0.3 (z -20.1), resolving the zero-divisor sign of the certified sedenion kernel (the eigenvalue -1 of L_e1^T L_e10) at both angles, while the bright vector's odd part read -0.016 +- 0.009, within one standard error of its modeled -0.008 (H2 z -0.92). The sine-law contrast odd(0.3) - 2.84 odd(0.1) read +0.021 +- 0.026 (H3 z 0.78), the kernel even part +0.049 against its decomposition +0.046 (H4 z 0.33), and QB11's and QB12's prx trains fit relative over-rotations of +0.15 +- 0.07 % and -0.20 +- 0.06 % (H5 chi-square 5.1 and 1.1). No preregistered hypothesis is falsified. The visibility read 0.36 +- 0.05 against the model's 0.48, and the job charged 1.50 credits.
claims.boundary: One compile, one calibration set and two angles. The kernel-minus-bright double difference, the test the Tuna-17 run showed is needed, reads -0.0538 +- 0.0124 (z -4.3) at phi = 0.1, and -0.132 +- 0.026 (z -5.0) at 0.3 if the bright artifact scales like sin(2 phi), since the case ran the bright arm at phi = 0.1 only. The prediction schedules idle relaxation ALAP; scheduled ASAP, IQM's pulse-builder default, it would move H4 to about z -2.5 and H2 to z -0.3 with no decision changed (issue #386). cd_core already settles the zero-divisor property exactly, so the run demonstrates that Garnet realizes the compiled sign table at first order; the bright control and the sine law bound circuit artifacts, and the even part's agreement with readout plus relaxation leaves no room for the large coherent error the signed probe's offsets once suggested.

claims.statement: On the QX emulator the 18-circuit twin of the Tuna-17 kernel cancellation series (six batches of three: the same compiled arms on register qubits 0-4, control q1, 2048 shots each) read the kernel odd parts -0.1848 +- 0.0109 at phi = pi/36 and -0.4944 +- 0.0096 at pi/12 against the ideal -0.1736 and -0.5000, within 1.03 and 0.58 standard errors, and the bright odd part exactly 0, so the platform executes the emitted cQASM as compiled.
claims.boundary: An ideal emulator; it checks the emitted cQASM and the platform's handling of it, not device noise or the angle quantization of Tuna.

claims.statement: On Tuna-17 (region 4, 8, 11, 12, 14, 45 CZ, every rotation on the pi/36 grid, 32768 shots per arm over two batches), the kernel cancellation probe read kernel odd parts of -0.0222 +- 0.0039 at phi = pi/36 and -0.0547 +- 0.0039 at pi/12, but the bright vector, whose ideal odd part is zero, read -0.0167 +- 0.0039 (z -4.3): the preregistered H2 is falsified and the probe carries a signed response that does not depend on the kernel. The preregistered H1, the kernel against zero, resolves at pi/36 and is withheld at pi/12, whose contrast ran out of order; with H2 falsified, that resolution does not establish the zero-divisor sign. The sine-law test is withheld, since the series measures no bright control at pi/12.
claims.boundary: Six batches, each its own calibration context, pooled in pairs; one region and a bright arm at phi = pi/36 only, so the artifact at pi/12 is unmeasured. The platform runs each circuit as its own job in an order of its own: the provider start times show the pi/36 kernel and bright contrasts executed +, -, -, + as preregistered and the pi/12 kernel contrast +, -, +, -, a protocol deviation the analysis names. The bright response's mechanism (the non-unital relaxation that gives the bright arm a small odd part in the Garnet model, or a position effect that differs between a contrast's two batches) is untested on Tuna-17, which has no retained noise model.
assumptions: the two batches of a contrast carry the same within-batch position effect, so the +, -, -, + balance across them cancels it
a batch's readout assignment factor equals its batch pair's, whose two references sit in different batches; the spread of the series' readout references enters the corrected errors

claims.boundary: Selected after viewing the bright control, against the manifests' preregistered H1 of the kernel against zero; it holds under the main claim's position and readout assumptions, and a matched decision needs a case that preregisters it.

claims.statement: The preregistered stationarity case on qpu:belenos, four post-calibration jobs repeating the crossed BDSC diagnostic's frozen requests at 100000 samples per iteration with every returned circuit equal to its retained counterpart, reads its primary inconclusive under the frozen mode-5 detector_absent veto: the heterogeneity of matched block changes about their class means is 66.1 on 45 degrees of freedom (p 0.022; the subtract veto reads 65.0, p 0.027). The dark-click coincidence falsifier reads consistent (p 0.31), the superposition common shift reads +0.0003 (z 0.8) rather than repeating the retained -0.0044, and the superpositions keep an excess spread tau 0.0021 (interval 0.0009 to 0.0035) while f and g read none; the veto removes 0.999 of the superpositions' raw tau^2. Reported only: the mode-5 share fell from a block mean of 0.249 to 0.057 at a constant plan-time dark-count figure of 48440.3 counts/s, and the pre-calibration run of the b1-j1 requests against its repeat reads a superposition shift of -0.0017 (z -2.8) across the calibration.
claims.boundary: One device and one calibration, two blocks about an hour apart; the case separates neither slow drift from a step change nor drift within a window. Standard errors and p-values are reference values under independent Bernoulli trials, uncalibrated while the provider contract leaves count provenance unresolved. The calibration hold and the post-calibration repeat of b1-j1 were amendments committed before the jobs they govern; the pre-calibration b1-j1 run enters no frozen test. The plan-time dark-count figure is a platform reading, not an acquisition-time measurement, so the mode-5 mechanism stays a candidate. An inconclusive primary decides neither branch; it makes no certification decision.

claims.statement: Exact finite controls certify real-left normality at dimensions 2 through 64, the 4/8/4 sedenion Gram sectors, complete filter probability accounting, distinct order and associator references, phase and remote-ensemble invariance, finite embeddings and error-set-specific correction.
claims.boundary: The certificate covers its explicit operators, dimensions and instruments. Conditional filtering, a generic complex exceptional point and repeated projections establish no fundamental-physics departure, protected phase, physical squeezing or device benefit.

claims.statement: Seventeen logical circuits implement Design B dark/bright/quadrature controls, coherent/dephased/fixed-order controls, one/two/four-step measurement sequences with unmeasured and reset references, a heralded contraction and dimension-8/16/32 associator spectra; complete branch enumeration agrees with their declared laws within 1e-10 after portable-basis compilation.
claims.boundary: Finite numerical conformance without sampled jobs. Portable CX/RZ/SX/X compilation establishes neither native hardware routing nor a scheduler, cost or acquisition result.

claims.statement: Operational case contracts pair algebra-specific response, singular-sector dynamics, coherent selection, sequential measurement and effective nonunitarity with property-removing mutations, unconditional accounting and prospective calibration controls.
claims.boundary: Logical instruments and exact models are available. Fresh physical scheduling, block-level covariance and power, provider-specific costs and separate approval precede acquisition; squeezing, protected topology and quantum-code benefit remain capability- or definition-gated.

claims.statement: The preregistered drift series on qpu:belenos, seven unchanged resubmissions of the stationarity case's b1-j1 request two hours apart from 07:00Z to 19:00Z on 2026-10-24 (165 to 176 s each, every returned circuit equal to its retained counterpart), reads its primary consistent under the mode-5 detector_absent veto: the mean von Neumann ratio of the 16 class-centered superposition settings is 1.674 against 2 for exchangeable runs, exact permutation p 0.056 over all 5040 orderings (the independent-setting normal reference reads z -2.02, p 0.022, reported only). The superposition class mean shows no ordered common drift (ratio 2.02); qd-belenos-bdsc-drift-series-diagnostic records its unordered run-to-run jumps. Reported only: the class-centered excess square change of the superposition settings rises with lag, 7.1e-6 at 2 h to 2.1e-5 at 8 to 10 h and 2.2e-5 at 12 h, and the plan-time dark-count figure changes between every pair of runs (mode 5 from 7326.8 to 18616.3 counts/s), so no two runs share a calibration epoch and the within-epoch contrast is undefined.
claims.boundary: One device, one request set of 24 compilations, seven runs in one day; the primary's sensitivity is 0.71 for a random walk of step SD 0.0021 per two hours and 0.43 at 0.0015, so a consistent reading at p 0.056 leaves a walk of that size undecided rather than excluded. The lag profile of the excess is reported only: its points share runs and carry no independent error. The epoch rule assumed the platform refreshes the dark-count figures only at calibration; they changed every two hours, so the epochs it assigns name figure refreshes, not calibrations. Standard errors stay reference values under independent Bernoulli trials. The series certifies nothing about the case's other 72 settings.

claims.statement: Exploratory readings of the seven drift-series runs on qpu:belenos, chosen after the preregistered readout. The unweighted superposition class mean jumps between runs, 0.3928 to 0.4042 with sample SD 0.0038 against a counting error near 0.0004 per run, while its order carries no memory (von Neumann ratio 2.02). The class-centered pair excess, with the counting variance of the centered change subtracted, rises from 7.45e-6 at 2 h to 2.27e-5 at 12 h, and its Spearman correlation with lag over the 21 series pairs is 0.65, exact p 0.006 over all 5040 relabelings of the run times. All 56 six-state sum-rule contrasts (four template-and-seed groups, two sums, seven runs) are negative, -0.251 to -0.140 with mean -0.199, where every fixed linear effect gives zero. The mean mode-5 share does not follow the plan-time mode-5 dark rate (Spearman 0.15, two-sided p 0.71 over nine runs; -0.11, p 0.84 over the seven series runs).
claims.boundary: Every reading here was chosen after the preregistered readout and leaves its consistent primary unchanged; the lag-trend p is one of several statistics examined, so it names a candidate memory effect for a preregistered successor, not a resolved drift. Its relabeling null assumes exchangeable runs; the 21 pair excesses share runs. The centered counting variance assumes independent setting errors under the reference Bernoulli standard errors, while the four settings of one template and seed share a compilation. The sum-rule deficit extends the deficit the acceptance diagnostics already document on these banks; the banks are phase-blind, so the sums test intensity linearity of the conditioned response, not coherence.

claims.statement: The even gaps 20 (k = 6), 32 (k = 8), 86 and 88 (k = 14) are absent between consecutive integers coprime to the k-th primorial, each with defect exactly one: an allowed residue assignment leaves one uncovered point (wheel gaps 6 + 14, 6 + 26, 44 + 42, 58 + 30), exhaustive search over 4, 15, 1485 and 150 branch assignments finds no cover, and the next prime 17, 23, 47, 47 closes each gap. At k = 14 the fractional relaxation has optimum 0 with an exactly verified rational cover. Fixing the k = 14 witnesses except p = 5, 7, 11 gives cost tables with Walsh coefficients in (1/8)Z; the gap-86 repair by 22 mod 47 shifts its Hamiltonian by -I and the gap-88 repair by 29 mod 47 by -(I + Z1)/2.
claims.boundary: Four finite instances, matching Ziller's Table 1 (arXiv 2007.01808, p. 12); no bound on branching depth or gap growth as k increases and no bearing on Ziller's Conjecture 4.1.

claims.statement: Exhaustive restricted-cover search over every even difference from 2 to h(k) for k = 1..20 reproduces the missing differences and N_min(k) of every row of Ziller's Table 1 (arXiv 2007.01808v1, p. 12): the only missing differences are 20 (k = 6), 32 (k = 8), 86 and 88 (k = 14), 98 (k = 15), 146 (k = 19) and 166, 170 and 172 (k = 20), each excluded over 135 to 180 branch assignments of 3, 5, 7 and 11, and each of the other 628 cells has a verified cover; h(k) is in D(k) in every row.

Exclusions rest on the depth-first search and its capacity pruning, not on a separately checkable certificate; no bearing on rows k > 20 or Conjecture 4.1.

claims.statement: Under the ibm_kingston noise model of 2026-10-15T19:42:21-07:00 on its best and median three-qubit paths, with every arm ALAP scheduled, null-subtracted phase-gradient tomography of the eight-CNOT gap-88 cost recovers every coefficient within 0.0032 of its exact value (identification radius 1/16) at 2,803 and 3,169 shots per setting, the budget carrying each mean's variance through the assignment inversion and the null arm's phase variance; the gap-88 repair contrast reads -0.499 against -0.5, the gap-20 Grover quotient reads its marked label at 0.963 to 0.984, and the gap-86 repair leaves every compiled law unchanged. A noise-free CZ conditional phase of 0.02 to 0.1 rad per CZ biases the coefficients by 0.057 to 0.287 with cycle residuals at most 0.0103, and subtracting the zero-angle null arm reduces the bias to 0.0005 to 0.0128; a 10 to 30 kHz detuning of one path qubit biases them by 0.015 to 0.233, reaching multi-body coefficients through the parities its wire carries, and null subtraction leaves at most 0.0022; an sx amplitude error of 0.002 to 0.01 biases them by at most 0.0007.

claims.statement: On the best and median three-qubit ibm_kingston paths of the primorial noise record, the compiled gap-88 phase-gradient arms and their zero-angle null arms carry identical sx, x, cz and delay streams, differing only in zero-duration rz. Noise-free static ZZ of 2 to 20 kHz on both couplers (partner-in-0 and symmetric frames) biases the raw coefficients by up to 0.078 and the null-subtracted ones by at most 0.00038; a drive-axis tilt of 0.005 or 0.02 rad on one or all path qubits biases them by up to 0.174 raw and at most 0.0055 null-subtracted, both entering at second order; tilt at each path qubit's sx gate-error bound (0.021 to 0.036 rad) in the worst of eight sign patterns leaves 0.0147 (best) and 0.0159 (median) null-subtracted. Every residual stays below one standard deviation of the noisy null-subtracted estimate at the retained budget (0.0188 at 2,803 and 0.0186 at 3,169 shots per setting), so the circuits pose no primorial-specific device question on Heron r2.

claims.statement: On the best (45-46-47) and median (117-125-126) ibm_kingston paths of the primorial noise record, a numpy statevector of the compiled gap-88 phase-gradient and zero-angle null arms reproduces every retained null-residual and coherent-sensitivity scenario to 1.6e-15. Drive-axis tilt at each path qubit's sx gate-error bound and CZ conditional phase at each coupler's CZ bound (0.097 to 0.104 rad), applied jointly, leave a null-subtracted coefficient bias of 0.049 (best) and 0.050 (median), 2.61 and 2.84 standard deviations of that coefficient at the retained budgets, and identifying all seven coefficients at that bias takes 53,363 and 76,596 shots per setting against the retained 2,803 and 3,169; under the sx-and-x budget the joint residual is 1.90 and 2.06 standard deviations. Each family alone stays below one standard deviation (tilt 0.79 and 0.89, CZ phase 0.72 and 0.77). With tilt at 0.1 of its bound no CZ phase within its bound reaches one standard deviation (0.84 and 0.90); at 0.2 the full CZ bound reaches 0.98 and 1.04. claims.statement: On the best and median ibm_kingston paths of the primorial noise record, the coherence probes of gororoba_quantum/coherence_probes.py recover injected drive-axis tilt, CZ conditional phase, static detuning and partner-in-0 ZZ, every family at once, within 5.2e-5 rad of x tilt, 4.1e-5 rad of sx tilt, 3.8e-6 rad of CZ phase, 2.6 Hz of detuning and 1.3 Hz of ZZ; a constant-amplitude detuned pulse equals the tilt Delta / Omega to an infidelity of 3.6e-10 up to 60 kHz. Under the snapshot's noise each estimate's bias stays below its standard error, and the shots that resolve each decision threshold at three standard deviations are 2 for CZ phase at 0.7 of its bound, at most 18 for tilt at 0.2 of its sx and x bounds, at most 60 for 5 kHz detuning and 757 for 2 kHz ZZ. Thirty-two independent samplomatic twirl randomizations of the gap-88 signal and null arms raise the joint tilt and CZ-phase max_z at the gate-error bounds to 5.4 and 6.5 against 2.6 and 2.8 untwirled (512 randomizations: 1.03 and 1.11). claims.statement: For doubly pure y = (p, q) in A_n and z = p + i q, phi(y x) = A(z, conj z) conj(phi(x)) with A(z, t) = [[0, -t^T], [t, C_z]], so rank_R L_y = 2 rank_C A(z, conj z); the cofactors of C_z satisfy P_j = f_n z_j for a homogeneous f_n in Z[z] of degree 2^(n-2) - 2, and det L_y = N^4 |f_n(z)|^4, with f_4 = Q and f_5 = Q G.
claims.boundary: Written proof for every n in docs/evidence/stiefel-pfaffian-higher/README.md; gate core-692 checks the transport on every basis pair at n = 6 and 7 and the cofactor identities at n = 6, 7, 8, and the independent verification (verification.md) re-derived the proof and checked n = 8 with its own code. The degree-(2^(n-2) - 2) form of f_n beyond n = 8 rests on the written argument only; not formalized in Rocq.
assumptions: cd_core.cd_sign doubling convention (a, b)(c, d) = (ac - conj(d) b, da + b conj(c))

claims.statement: For n = 6, 7, 8, f_n is irreducible over Q and not divisible by Q = z.z, so the zero-divisor Stiefel elements of A_n form the complex points of V(Q, f_n), a cone of pure real dimension 2^n - 6, codimension 2 in the Stiefel cone; on unit pairs the dimension is 57, 121 and 249. The five-term element e_12 + e_15 + e_16 + e_23 + 2 e_34 is an invertible Stiefel element of A_6.
claims.boundary: Irreducibility by a mod-p line argument in gate core-692 and, independently, by an exact factorization over Z on an integer line (verification.md); the dimension follows from Krull's principal ideal theorem on the irreducible quadric cone V(Q) because z = p + i q covers all of C^(2^(n-1) - 1). Given Biss-Christensen-Dugger-Isaksen Theorem 1.5, V(Q, f_6) contains the component {Q = z_16 = 0} and at least one other, through e_16 + i e_1 (nullity 28). Every Stiefel element of A_6 supported on at most four coordinates is a zero divisor by an exact slice computation in the ungated --explore record, not by a gate. Open: f_n modulo Q, absolute irreducibility, the number and real structure of components, and least supports at A_7 and A_8.
assumptions: cd_core.cd_sign doubling convention (a, b)(c, d) = (ac - conj(d) b, da + b conj(c))
Biss, Christensen, Dugger and Isaksen, math/0702075, Theorem 1.5, for the component statement only

claims.statement: Moreno's question has a negative answer at A_7 and A_8: an explicit disjoint-support integer Stiefel element has left multiplication of exact rank 128 and 256, so it is not a zero divisor.
claims.boundary: Exact integer ranks of the two retained witnesses, re-derived by gate core-692 and independently by the verification; nothing beyond the two elements.
assumptions: cd_core.cd_sign doubling convention (a, b)(c, d) = (ac - conj(d) b, da + b conj(c))

claims.statement: Open: the form of f_n modulo Q for n >= 6, whether f_n lies in (Q, z_s^2) with s = 2^(n-2), and whether f_n is absolutely irreducible.
claims.boundary: f_n does not lie in (Q, z_s^3) for n = 6, 7 (isotropic lines over F_p, verification row 7b); membership in (Q, z_s^2) holds on two coordinate slices and on every tested line, which proves nothing beyond them.
assumptions: cd_core.cd_sign doubling convention (a, b)(c, d) = (ac - conj(d) b, da + b conj(c))

claims.statement: On ibm_kingston (calibration 2026-10-25T12:18:10-07:00, executed on physical qubits 106, 105, 104, 117, 107, 125 for r, d0, d1, d2, a0, a1; one job of 34 dynamic PUBs at 16384 shots) a single conditional X recovers an injected X error on a bit-flip-coded Bell pair: F(ff_0) - null is 0.745 [0.699, 0.790] and F(ff_0) - F(unencoded) is 0.553 [0.507, 0.598]. The controller latency and the conditional cost no resolved fidelity beyond their idle: frame_0 - ff_0 reads 0.010 [-0.035, 0.055] and frame_l - ff_0 reads -0.004 [-0.049, 0.041]. A requested 10 us idle, executed as 9.748 us on the feed-forward path (the broadcast overlaps the delay) and 10.000 us on the frame path per the returned scheduler_timing, costs 0.217 [0.172, 0.262] and 0.223 [0.178, 0.268], against 0.082 and 0.079 predicted from the calibrated T1 and T2: a finite-window slope of 0.022 per us on both paths, and -ln(F(W)/F(0)) of 0.033 to 0.034 per us. Descriptively, about 0.12 of that loss is a -0.81 rad rotation of the four-qubit block (near -13 kHz) and the rest a coherence decay with time constant 38 to 40 us against 65 to 67 us predicted.
claims.boundary: One layout, one calibration and one job; Hoeffding intervals at alpha 0.05/7 per endpoint. The +-0.01 equivalence margins of latency_is_idle and window_slope are not reached, so equal cost is bounded, not shown. The phase and the decay time constants come from the summary expectations and were not preregistered beyond decay_not_phase; the detuning's source is undecided. A bit-flip code protects no phase. Layout search and model sampling used the runner's reproduction seeds, not a QRNG draw; the runner took no seed at run time then (issue #514). Two exposures cannot decide whether the fidelity decays exponentially, so -ln(F(W)/F(0)) is a rate of an exponential law only under that assumption.

claims.statement: On ibm_kingston (calibration 2026-10-25T13:27:48-07:00; one job of 19 dynamic PUBs at 8192 shots over 14 disjoint pairs with both readout errors at most 1 percent) the record-steered rotation of the two-qubit QET ladder does not lower Bob's local energy below the floor -<H_A>: the mean channel floor margin over pairs is -0.160 +- 0.052 (one-sided 95 percent lower bound -0.252) against +0.057 from the calibration-noise model. Feed-forward executes the selected branch: the feedback arm's local energy 0.159 equals the record-binned fixed arms' 0.164 and q_eff has median -0.049 across pairs. The product-state mutation reads -0.307 +- 0.010 and the ground-minus-product margin drop +0.147 (lower bound +0.066). The shortfall tracks the prepared parity <Z_A Z_B> (correlation 0.961 across pairs), 0.874 pooled against 1.
claims.boundary: One calibration, one job, 14 pairs placed under a 1 percent readout cap, t-intervals across pairs. Energies are expectations of an encoded spin Hamiltonian, not field stress-energy. The margin result concerns this operating point (14 simultaneous captures, 2.83 us measure-to-branch wait). Layout search and model sampling used the runner's reproduction seeds.

claims.statement: On the same 14 ibm_kingston pairs (calibration 2026-10-25T15:17:22-07:00, 24 dynamic PUBs at 8192 shots) the ladder's parity loss is a phase on B over the measure-to-branch idle that the service scheduler places inside the preparation CX: the parity is equal with and without Alice's readout during the 722 dt wait (difference -0.001 +- 0.004), completing the CX first restores the parity to 0.965 +- 0.002 and moves the phase onto <X_A X_B> pair by pair (0.998 against 0.862 rad on [149, 150]), and the service schedules a branch-target qubit's pre-branch operations at the broadcast receive, so an X echo written before the branch played after the window and left the phase unchanged. A per-pair fit of delta Z_B / 2 + zeta Z_A Z_B / 2 plus dephasing to the deferred-frame observables gives delta from -54 to +11 kHz and zeta from 1.5 to 14 kHz.

The scheduler rule is read from this job's returned scheduler_timing and may change with the service.

claims.statement: With Bob's record-independent rz(alpha) fixed per pair from that pair's own reference arms (grid -0.3 to +1.2 rad), the 14 ibm_kingston pairs show an information excess of +0.107 +- 0.006 (one-sided 95 percent lower bound +0.096) against the ideal E_B = 0.115: the record lowers Bob's local energy below every record-independent unitary on the same preparation. The channel floor margin stays negative at -0.073 +- 0.015 (lower bound -0.100), because the reference state's best uninformed local energy is 0.177 above the vacuum value. A 50 us repetition delay charged 12 s for 147,456 shots (81 us per shot against 276 us at 250 us) and left assignment, parity and coherence unchanged on 11 of 14 pairs.

The repetition-delay comparison spans two jobs 25 minutes apart, so drift and delay are not separated on the three pairs that moved. One calibration, one job.

claims.statement: The service schedule of the encoded N=21 Kingston run leaves leaf qubits 104, 106, 124 and 126 idle for 14,323 to 15,481 dt (57 to 62 us of a 70 us circuit) behind their hubs' CZ chains, in both arms; NoiseModel.from_backend charges relaxation on gates and explicit delays only, so the model charged that idle nothing. With the scheduled idle written in as delays under the execution Target and the declared initial excitation 0.014393, the exact branch-resolved contrast difference moves from +0.0310 (the unpadded control reproduces the record's exact model to 1e-15) to -0.0007, inside the measured 95 % interval [-0.0129, +0.0184], and the law distance to hardware falls from 0.0216 to 0.0129 TV (feedback) and from 0.0273 to 0.0158 TV (omitted correction). A list schedule under the Target durations alone predicts the service idle within 5 % on every leaf qubit and 11 % on the hubs, so the idle is predictable before submission.

A contrast near zero follows from any added decoherence, so the replay's support is its absence of a fitted parameter and the law-distance reduction. The prospective test is a placement or routing that halves the leaf idle, predicted from a local schedule before submission.

claims.statement: Replaying the three ibm_kingston QET jobs exactly with the service-scheduled idle written in as delays under the execution Target, incoherent idle moves the ladder channel floor margin from +0.057 to +0.001 (measured -0.160), the frame diagnostic's as-run parity from 0.982 to 0.960 (measured 0.863) and the compensated selected margin from +0.057 to +0.028 (measured -0.073), and produces no window phase (0.010 rad padded against 0.267 measured). The phase that empties the uncompensated information excess (padded 0.099, measured 0.019) is therefore coherent and outside the Target's T1 and T2; once each pair's reference arms compensate it, the measured information excess 0.107 agrees with both the padded exact 0.112 and the unpadded exact 0.105, an endpoint insensitive to the incoherent idle.

claims.statement: On ibm_kingston (calibration 2026-10-25T19:36:09-07:00; one static job of six PUBs at 8192 shots over 38 pairwise uncoupled qubits, 15 s charged) the readout-corrected P0 of the 32-sx unitary sequence at N = 16 differs from the pinching analysis's sign-pooled Bloch-iteration prediction by a root-mean-square of 0.0152 over all 38 informative qubits, 0.0188 over the eight main qubits and 0.0141 over the thirty further qubits, against a statistical root-mean-square standard error of 0.0024. The preregistered floor, the larger of the all-qubit and main-qubit values, is 0.018784. The mean residual is +0.0110: the model underpredicts P0 on 32 of 38 qubits (all eight main qubits), by up to +0.039 on q91 and +0.034 on q45, and overpredicts it on six. The residual does not follow T2 in the drive-dephasing lead's direction: its Spearman correlation with T2 is -0.29 (two-sided p 0.080; 9 of the 12 longest-T2 qubits positive, 2 of the 12 shortest negative) and with the sx error -0.33 (p 0.044).
claims.boundary: One calibration window, one job, one backend; the floor is the root-mean-square of a model residual that includes counting noise, and it measures the sign-even part of the gate-model error because the pooled unitary arm is blind to the first-order axis tilt. The mean residual is positive, so the model underpredicts P0 systematically on this device and the floor mixes a common offset (+0.011) with qubit-to-qubit scatter. The correlations come from 38 qubits chosen by readout error, rank-based with a t-approximation p value, and are descriptive: the T2 test does not support the Garnet drive-dephasing lead and neither establishes a mechanism nor excludes one. The model takes the Target T1 at execution and the planning excitation, not a fit.

claims.statement: The single-chip teleportation rehearsal on qpu:belenos, job 55479252-d907-45ac-b1e1-84f19d21a131 submitted 2026-10-26 02:54:50 UTC under the anchor gate (model pooled fidelity 0.868 at the 2026-10-24 anchor figures, 0.635 at the held live figures), completed in 292 s and returned 0 three-click samples in each of its six iterations, each reporting its full max_shots of 1,200,000 as nb_shots_used. claims.statement: On ibm_kingston (execution calibration 2026-10-26T14:25:32-07:00; one job of 44 dynamic PUBs at 4096 shots and a 20 us repetition delay over 31 coupled pairs, 62 qubits) the relaxation multiplier kappa_1 = Gamma_1 T1_reported has median 1.057 [0.978, 1.183], so the preregistered optimistic-T1 decision reads absent or unresolved; Ramsey decay runs faster than the reported Hahn-echo T2 (kappa_2* median 1.451 [1.276, 1.905]) and faster than the measured echo decay (ratio 1.269 [1.170, 1.330], echo gain present); and the readout of every replica's partner during a probe's 40 us idle changes the probe's Ramsey phase rate by -2.72 +- 0.53 kHz against the after arm and -2.73 +- 0.54 kHz against the quiet Ramsey arm in the pair mean, with the quiet null at -0.010 +- 0.020 kHz (decision present). Reading the window-dose sweep's residual as this precession carries the mechanism across a different calibration and instance.

A matched returned mesh does not establish identical applied analog controls; elapsed time, calibration and source or detector response can confound the comparison, and changes of comparable size are already recorded between jobs minutes apart in different contexts, so the 33-hour difference is not attributed to drift.

claims.statement: The frozen Ascella predecessor case, run on sim:ascella with only its job name and platform substituted (job 51c0552b), returns all eight iterations at 32,768 events each, 3 of the 262,144 events outside single-photon eligibility. The signed common target-slot contrast norm is 153/65536 (0.0023) and the reversal norm 71/65536 (0.0011). The simulator carries no predecessor memory, so these contrasts measure the analysis pipeline's level at zero memory on sim:ascella and say nothing about the device's response; the differing computed circuits show that sim:ascella compiles the case differently from the QPU.

claims.statement: Physical 16-setting octonion associator character execution on qpu:ascella and twin simulation on sim:ascella route the encoded octonion character of each pair into the predicted harmonic mode: raw unconditional output mode fidelity over all 12 detected modes is 98.08% to 99.60% on the four octonion-arm settings (mean 98.75%) and 98.03% to 99.78% over all 16 settings (mean 99.22%), the conditional character contrast on the {0, omega} subspace is Delta_char = 1.997074, and sentinel mode leakage across modes 8..11 is 0.4888%.

Raw mode fidelity accounts for all 12 detected physical output modes including 0.49% sentinel leakage and 0.76% cross-talk, whereas conditional contrast is evaluated strictly on the {0, omega} logical subspace.

claims.statement: The 21-pair, 84-setting single-photon character atlas on qpu:ascella (10,000 samples per setting, 840,000 in all) and its sim:ascella twin route every octonion pair's encoded character into its predicted mode omega(a, b): on the QPU the octonion arm reads D from 0.9944 to 0.9996 and the reversed arm 0.9956 to 0.9996, the Clifford control and diagonal null arms route to mode 0 (D -1.000 to -0.9944 and -1.000 to -0.9973), the mean character contrast is 1.997448 and sentinel leakage is 1.3156%; raw unconditional mode fidelity spans 89.17% to 99.84% over the 84 settings (mean 98.28%). The twin reads D = +-1.000000 on every setting with zero leakage.

Contrasts are conditional on the {0, omega} subspace; the fidelity figure counts every detected output mode.

claims.statement: The two-photon, 84-setting character atlas on sim:ascella (2,030 two-click events per setting, 170,520 in all) routes both photons into each displacing pair's predicted focal coset pair (mean displacing contrast 2.0) and keeps the stabilizer-line pairs in (0, 2) (mean persistence 1.0), with zero sentinel leakage; it is the simulator twin of the qpu:ascella atlas whose job awaits collection.

claims.statement: On sim:belenos the six packed box-kite jobs (32 one-photon sign blocks, 20000 to 60001 samples per job) return every dark block at a = 0 and every bright block at a = 1 with no violating sample, and the 16 half blocks at a = 0.488 to 0.515 (mean 0.4996) against the exact 1/2.
claims.boundary: A simulator reproduces the preregistered ideals; it carries no device error, so it qualifies the packed case and the analysis rather than the chip. Under the binomial standard error at 1/2 over each block's one-click samples, 3 of the 16 half blocks lie beyond two standard errors (+2.56, +2.71 and -2.20) and the largest deviation is 0.0149; this is descriptive sampling scatter, not a bound on simulator bias.

claims.statement: On qpu:belenos the same six packed jobs (60000 shots per job, the last 20000) read the 8 dark blocks at a = 0.005 to 0.050 (mean 0.033) and the 8 bright blocks at a = 0.863 to 0.994 (mean 0.960), so the t sign flip that turns each zero product x y = 0 into a bright product moves the algebra fraction by 0.93 on average against the ideal 1; the 16 half blocks read 0.405 to 0.619 (mean 0.511) against 1/2, up to 19.8 binomial standard errors from 1/2.
claims.boundary: The jobs ran without a preregistered decision rule, so every figure is descriptive. In a packed job each block holds about one sixth of the one-click samples, so in_block is a share across blocks and not the single-block routing fidelity of the earlier Belenos claims. The dark floor mixes dark counts, multiphoton emission and mesh error, which this design does not separate.

claims.statement: Every circuit of the Tuna-17 DeMarrais campaign is H on all 17 qubits, Tuna-17's 18 native CZ couplers, X on two to four hub qubits, the same CZ layer and H, so its ideal outcome is the CZ-neighbour parity of the X'd hubs; pauli_propagation.py derives all nine ideal strings from the edge list and hubs and matches the exact statevector and each manifest. Over 75536 shots per circuit (nine jobs, 1642194 to 1642318) the data qubits with an odd number of X'd neighbours (ideal 1) read a mean P(1) of 0.67 to 0.86 and those with none (ideal 0) 0.26 to 0.41, the full 17-bit string matches on 0.9 to 1.4 % of shots, and the all-zero sentinel herald keeps 11 to 16 %.
claims.boundary: The circuits carry no Cayley-Dickson content: the 8192D, 4096D and 32D labels select only which qubits receive X on one shared CZ graph, cd_core enters no gate, and no circuit changes its ideal outcome when an algebraic property is removed, so the campaign fails the repository's mutation test and measures Tuna-17's fidelity on a two-layer 36-CZ Clifford circuit. Two-path extinction is Z Z = I on a qubit with two X'd neighbours. The sleeper null removes the X gates and so tests readout bias and Pauli propagation, not algebra. The herald selects shots whose nine sentinels all read 0, about 0.79^9 of them, which raises the heralded contrast by error detection.

claims.statement: On the Quantum Inspire QX simulator the nine 10-qubit DeMarrais circuits (one 10-edge CZ graph, X on zero to four hubs, 2048 shots each) return their CZ-neighbour parity string on every shot, the exact outcome pauli_propagation.py derives from each circuit's edges and hubs.
claims.boundary: A noiseless simulator of a Clifford circuit with one deterministic outcome reproduces that outcome by construction; it qualifies the cases and the analysis, and the 1024D labels set no gate.

claims.statement: On sim:belenos job 0866fc0c (job-dm4, 24 settings at 10000 samples each) returned its first nine settings, the 16D to 4096D midden-quotient controls, each at the ideal dispersive contrast D = 1.0 with no click above the lower 12 modes, and then failed at the first 8192D setting with 'RuntimeError: Circuit optimizer: No trial converged' (90000 samples, 90004 shots); the remaining fourteen settings, every 8192D and null arm among them, returned nothing.
claims.boundary: A simulator run qualifies the case and the provider's compiler, not a device. With no null arm returned the analysis withholds a verdict. The returned controls send one photon through a 12-mode quotient unitary whose ideal outcome is a basis-mode routing, so their agreement tests compilation, not a zero-divisor property.

claims.statement: On ibm_fez (calibration 2026-10-29T15:59:57-07:00; backup instance, one static job at 8192 shots over 47 pairwise uncoupled qubits, 15 s billed) the readout-corrected P0 of the 32-sx unitary sequence at N = 16 differs from the pinching analysis's Bloch-iteration prediction by a root-mean-square of 0.0338 over all 47 informative qubits, 0.0390 over the 24 main qubits and 0.0273 over the 23 further qubits, against a statistical root-mean-square of 0.0028. The preregistered floor, the larger of the all-qubit and main-qubit values, is 0.039015, about twice ibm_kingston's 0.018784. The mean residual is +0.020, and the residual's Spearman correlation with T2 is -0.35 (two-sided p 0.015) and with the sx error 0.003 (p 0.98).
claims.boundary: One calibration window, one job, one backend; the floor includes counting noise and measures the sign-even part of the gate-model error. The negative T2 correlation runs against the drive-dephasing lead's direction, as on ibm_kingston, and is descriptive over qubits chosen by readout error; it establishes no mechanism.

claims.statement: On 24 ibm_fez qubits (backup instance, one dynamic job of 101 PUBs at 5600 shots and a 20 us repetition delay, 31 s billed against 27.2 s planned) the successor analysis keeps no qubit and withholds the device verdict: the in-circuit reader carryover D is a median 0.019 (0.012 to 0.030) on all 20 qubits that reach the screen against a 0.0047 margin, and it tracks the single-reset control (median 0.017, ratio 1.14). The carryover between consecutive pattern rows is 0.00061 +- 0.00008 on the 20 pattern-passing qubits, three times ibm_kingston's 0.00020 +- 0.00006. A failed measure-and-flip reset is followed, at the same shot index of the next PUB, by a read of 1 with probability 0.081 (237/2925) against 0.0024 after a successful one (z 66); qubits 23, 95, 121, 147 and 151 carry that persistence, and ibm_kingston shows the same at 0.065 against 0.0033 (z 74) on qubits 50, 59, 62, 95, 100 and 154. The excess is absent at shot offsets 1, 2, 10 and 100 and strikes qubits independently.
claims.boundary: Runtime guarantees neither the PUB order nor a single batch and the run records no per-shot time, so the persistence and cross-shot figures pair shots by index, and the separation in time between paired shots is unmeasured. The reader screen bounds the residue of one reset, not the carryover after init_qubits, so its failure on Heron r2 was predictable from the 2026-10-27 Kingston reset control; the pinching question stays open. The persistence and carrier rows are exploratory reanalyses of the raw bits. Leakage outside the computational subspace and a repeating readout fault both fit the persistence; the twice-misread counts favor the readout fault without excluding leakage. The run record's ideal_laws were restored from the approved record by content digest after collection refused the as-submitted record.
